paper.title: A coronavirus protease activates sensory neurons via TRPA1 to drive sneeze, cough, and pain.
paper.abstract: Sneezing, coughing, and pain are common symptoms of respiratory viral infection. These responses are initiated by airway-innervating nociceptors that detect noxious stimuli, but how SARS-CoV-2 activates these neurons remains unclear. Here, we show that the coronavirus papain-like protease (PLpro) directly activates airway-innervating nociceptors in mice and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived nociceptors. PLpro triggers sneezing, coughing, acute pain, and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release in the airways. Both the proteolytic activity of PLpro and the host ion channel transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) are required for neuronal activation and sneezing. Infection with the mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 or the murine coronavirus MHV-A59 also induces sneezing in mice, and MHV-A59-evoked sneezing is TRPA1-dependent. SARS-CoV-2 infection of the trigeminal ganglia altered transcriptional programs associated with nociception, including upregulation of the TRPA1-CGRP signaling pathway activated by PLpro. Together, these findings reveal a direct mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 triggers pain and airway reflexes and identify PLpro and TRPA1 as potential therapeutic targets for COVID-19.

paper.title: Natural Bitter Compounds, Intestinal TAS2Rs, and GLP-1 Secretion: Mechanistic Evidence and Translational Challenges.
paper.abstract: Bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) are expressed beyond the oral cavity, and those in the intestine have been implicated in metabolic regulation. Selected natural bitter compounds (NBCs) increase glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) release in experimental enteroendocrine models, but predicted ligand binding, functional receptor activation, and receptor-dependent hormone secretion do not provide equivalent evidence. Intestinal TAS2Rs may thus provide a route to endogenous GLP-1 modulation distinct from receptor agonist therapy. Unlike broader reviews of extraoral chemosensing, this review maps these distinct endpoints for individual NBC-TAS2R pairs and separates measured GLP-1 release from changes in proglucagon expression. We define a receptor-supported enteroendocrine core and distinguish it from indirect evidence and testable hypotheses concerning microbiota-associated, immune-endocrine, and gut-brain interfaces. Receptor-directed perturbation supports selected compound-specific secretory responses, whereas the three proposed interfaces lack complete NBC-TAS2R-GLP-1 causal chains. We critically compare human-derived cell lines, animal models, primary tissues, and organoids, and summarize the experimental concentrations and GLP-1 assay endpoints where reported. Finally, we identify priorities for receptor-selective validation, measurement of intestinal target-site exposure, and prospective human studies. This evidence map clarifies what is experimentally supported and what must be demonstrated before intestinal TAS2Rs can be considered reliable targets for endogenous GLP-1 modulation.

paper.title: Functional Deficits and Diffusion Tensor Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Olfactory and Vision Systems in the Alzheimer's Disease Model of Aging GluN3A Knockout Mice.
paper.abstract: Sensory dysfunction, such as olfactory and visual deficits, is a notorious symptom during the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and related dementia (ADRD). The causal factor/s and structural disruptions underlying the sensory dysfunction in the AD/ADRD brain are not well understood. The NMDA receptor subunit GluN3A (NR3A) negatively regulates the receptor activity to uphold cellular Ca2+ homeostasis. In GluN3A knockout (KO) mice, animals spontaneously develop chronic neurodegenerative excitotoxicity, cognitive decline, and AD-like pathology. Using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), we examined neuronal network destruction together with sensory dysfunction in the GluN3A KO mouse. Specific attention was given to the selective vulnerability of the olfactory and visual nuclei, white matter injury in regional connections between subcortical centers and the cortex and hippocampus. Compared to age-matched wild-type (WT) controls (male), consistent with our early reports in younger ages, 18-month-old aging/aged GluN3A KO mice (male) suffered significant olfactory, visual and social deficits, accompanied by marked Aβ42 deposition in the brain. Ex vivo MR images of the GluN3A KO and control brains were acquired on the 7T MRI system, using a four-channel mouse array RF coil. High-resolution 3D T2-weighted RARE anatomical and DTI scans were performed. The DTI analysis revealed that GluN3A KO mice developed brain atrophy, involving significant damage in the white and gray matter of the olfactory and visual systems and impaired pathways among the superior colliculus, lateral geniculate nucleus, and the hippocampus and/or the cortex. This investigation disclosed a receptor-mediated neurodegeneration that explains sensory syndromes featured in a sporadic AD mouse model.

paper.title: Dietary Capsaicin Protects Against Obesity via a Microbiome-Dependent Mechanism Independent of Host TRPV1 Signalling.
paper.abstract: Background/Objectives: Dietary compounds simultaneously act on host tissue and gut microbiota, complicating efforts to distinguish direct host-receptor mechanisms from microbiome-mediated effects. Using a common food ingredient as proof-of-principle, this study aims to disentangle capsaicin host receptor signalling from capsaicin-microbiome interactions to determine the role of the gut microbiome in capsaicin-mediated metabolic protection. Methods: We employed a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity model with or without capsaicin supplementation in TRPV1 knockout mice to determine the role of the host receptor. We also depleted the gut microbiota with antibiotics to determine the role of the microbiome. Host metabolic phenotypes were monitored, and microbiome 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics were analysed and extended with functional prediction and machine learning algorithms, followed by functional validation in vivo. Results: Capsaicin supplementation significantly protected against HFD-induced obesity, even capsaicin receptor knockout hosts. Crucially, depletion of the microbiota abolished this metabolic protection, demonstrating the microbiome's obligatory role. While capsaicin supplementation did not alter hosts' cumulative food intake, dietary preferences, or energy expenditure, it induced significant shifts in gut microbial diversity and function and triggered extensive faecal metabolomic remodelling which indicate altered nutrient processing including dampened lipid absorption. Consistent with this finding, in vivo functional validation also reveals attenuated circulating lipid response following oral fat administration, and this effect of capsaicin is abrogated without the microbiome. Conclusions: Although capsaicin is well-recognised as a modulator of host appetite and metabolism via canonical host receptor signalling, our strategic use of a host knockout has enabled us to unmask a nuanced microbiome-modulatory role of this chilli pepper ingredient: capsaicin tweaks the microbiome to potentially dial down host fat absorption and protect against high-fat diet-induced obesity. We also highlight a generalisable host knockout experimental framework for distinguishing microbiome-mediated pathways versus direct host receptor mechanisms.

paper.title: Taste-like perception of citrus essential oils: Roles of taste receptors and retronasal aroma-taste integration.
paper.abstract: Citrus essential oils (EOs) can evoke taste-like perceptions, but whether these arise from direct taste receptor activation or aroma-driven flavor perception remains unclear. This study evaluated grapefruit and orange EOs using human taste receptor assays, volatile profiling, and nose-clip check-all-that-apply (CATA) sensory analysis. Neither EO activated umami, sweet, salty, or sour taste pathways, including TAS1R1/TAS1R3, TAS1R2/TAS1R3, ENaC, and OTOP1. Grapefruit EO activated multiple bitter taste receptors, whereas orange EO activated only TAS2R8. GC-MS analysis showed limonene-dominant volatile profiles in both EOs and grapefruit-specific constituents, including nootkatone, carvone-related compounds, and β-caryophyllene. Sourness selection increased significantly without a nose clip, despite the absence of detectable OTOP1 activation. These findings suggest that citrus EO-induced taste-like perception is attribute-dependent, with grapefruit bitterness associated with TAS2R activation and citrus sourness shaped mainly by retronasal aroma. This integrated approach provides a framework for distinguishing receptor-mediated taste activity from aroma-driven flavor perception in citrus flavor systems.

paper.title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory-Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing.
paper.abstract: Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory-mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision-denied environments. Yet current olfactory-mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co-localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self-assembled odor-sensitive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF-hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent-field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low-crosstalk olfactory-mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine-learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed-loop anemotactic navigation and multi-target odor tracing in complex three-dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

paper.title: Effect of olfactory stimulation with breast milk on pain and salivary cortisol responses to heel sticking in premature infants: a randomized controlled trial.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain stimuli may increase both oxygen consumption and stress hormone production, thereby hindering the physiological and neurological development of preterm infants. In this study, we investigated the impact of breast milk odor on pain scores, crying time, and salivary cortisol concentrations in preterm infants undergoing heel lances.

METHODS: A two-arm, double-blinded, randomized controlled trial was conducted (NCT05557435). Preterm infants in the experimental group received breast milk odor. Participants in the control group received distilled water odor. The Premature Infant Pain Profile-Revised (PIPP-R), crying time, and salivary cortisol concentration were evaluated at the baseline (T0), during the heel lance procedure (T1), and 25 min after the heel stick (T2). Data were analyzed using t-test, generalized estimating equation, and Bayesian linear regression.

RESULTS: In total, 64 participants were enrolled. At T1, the experimental group demonstrated a significantly lower mean PIPP-R score (10.2 ± 1.8) compared to the control group (11.9 ± 3.0) (95% confidence interval [CI]: -2.892, -0.426, t = - 2.690, p = 0.009). The crying time (152.3 ± 76.1 vs. 163.9 ± 72.2 s) was shorter, and the salivary cortisol concentration change difference between groups was not statistically significant (mean difference 3.6, 95% CI: -2.355, 9.544, t = 1.226, p = 0.228). The Bayesian linear regression showed that infants in the breast milk odor group had a significantly greater reduction in pain scores than those in the usual care group (β = 1.44, 95% CI: 0.16, 2.73). In addition, a greater number of previous painful experiences was significantly associated with a greater reduction in pain scores (β = -0.47, 95% CI: -0.92, -0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Provision of breast milk odor is a non-invasive, safe intervention for alleviating procedural pain in preterm infants. Providing breast milk odor is recommended alongside routine swaddling and environmental control to reduce stress and pain.

paper.title: Organization and remodeling of olfactory subsystems across development in the brilliant-thighed poison frog Allobates femoralis.
paper.abstract: Olfaction is important for many ecological and social behaviors, but the development, organization, and molecular features of the olfactory system remain poorly understood in most anuran amphibians. Understanding developmental changes is particularly important because, during metamorphosis, the olfactory system must adapt to the very different conditions encountered by aquatic larvae and mainly terrestrial adults. In the brilliant-thighed poison frog Allobates femoralis, chemical cues influence behavior during both aquatic and terrestrial life stages, but the organization of its olfactory system has not yet been described. Here, we examined the anatomy and molecular features of the olfactory system of A. femoralis during development. We identified a main olfactory epithelium and a vomeronasal organ, together with a distinct buccal-exposed olfactory epithelium that is present only in larvae. We also found an additional larval sensory epithelium that is in close connection to the main olfactory epithelium. The different sensory epithelia showed distinct anatomical features and projected to defined regions of the main and accessory olfactory bulb. Immunohistochemistry revealed Gαo-expressing receptor neurons in all these epithelia, together with Gαo-positive axonal projections to the main and accessory olfactory bulb. Our study provides the first detailed description of the developing olfactory system of A. femoralis. These findings provide a basis for future studies linking the organization and function of the olfactory system to the olfaction-guided behaviors of this species.

paper.title: Perceptual validation and receptor-level modeling of odorant evolution during the first decade of Pu-erh ripened tea storage.
paper.abstract: Volatile evolution in Pu-erh ripened tea stored for 1-10 years was characterized using headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, odor activity value (OAV), aroma recombination and omission experiment, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations were employed. Volatile composition differed markedly between samples stored for 1-5 and 6-10 years, and 103 volatile compounds were identified. Thirty-three compounds had OAVs>1, and 29 significantly affected aroma in omission tests. Partial least-squares discriminant analysis identified seven potential storage-discriminating volatiles, including linalool oxide II (pyranoid), linalool oxide I (furanoid), and 1,2,3-trimethoxybenzene. Molecular docking indicated hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions were predicted to contribute to odorant-receptor interactions, while dynamics simulations confirmed complex stability. This study provides a theoretical basis for investigating the perceptual validation and receptor-level modeling of odorant evolution during the storage of PRT.

paper.title: Ancient Schwannoma of the Nasal Cavity Arising From the Piriform Aperture: A Rare Case Report.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Schwannoma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumour arising from Schwann cells. Although head and neck schwannomas are common, their occurrence in the sinonasal tract is rare. Ancient schwannoma is an uncommon histopathological variant characterised by long-standing degenerative changes. Owing to its rarity and nonspecific clinical and radiological presentation, ancient schwannoma poses a diagnostic challenge.

CASE REPORT: We report the case of a 36-year-old man with a five-year history of nasal obstruction, initially left-sided and subsequently bilateral, associated with hyposmia progressing to anosmia, epistaxis, left-sided serous rhinorrhoea and headache. Nasal endoscopy revealed a bilobed, smooth-surfaced mass occupying the left nasal cavity. A preliminary biopsy was non-diagnostic; therefore, complete endoscopic excision was performed. Histopathological examination revealed an ancient schwannoma characterised by predominantly hypocellular Antoni B areas, the absence of cytological atypia and mitotic activity, a sclerohyaline stroma, and foci of intralesional osseous metaplasia. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for S100 and SOX10, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of <1%. The postoperative course was uneventful. At the 15-month follow-up, the patient's symptoms had completely resolved, with no evidence of disease recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Ancient schwannoma of the nasal cavity is a rare entity that should be considered in the differential diagnosis of benign sinonasal masses. Radiological findings are not pathognomonic; however, the presence of a well-circumscribed lesion with smooth bony remodelling and degenerative features may suggest a slow-growing benign process. Complete surgical excision, preferably via an endoscopic approach, is the treatment of choice and is associated with an excellent prognosis.

paper.title: Discrete functional regions of the olfactory bulb represent region-specific molecular feature sets.
paper.abstract: In the mammalian brain, odors are encoded by combinatorial activation of the glomeruli in the olfactory bulb. The topography of the bulb has been described as tunotopic or chemotopic, such that glomeruli with similar odor tuning or similar chemical property tuning are spatially close. However, several aspects of the bulb topography remain debated, in particular whether there are discrete regions of glomeruli with similar odor tuning, as opposed to a continuous tunotopic mapping, and whether commonly used molecular features have predictive power for the odor responses and are mapped to specific regions. Here, we measured glomerular odor responses in the mouse olfactory bulb by calcium imaging and analyzed the map between (1) the functional space of glomerular odor responses, (2) the two-dimensional bulb surface, and (3) the chemical space of molecular features. We found an organization of the bulb surface into discrete functional regions consisting of glomeruli with similar odor tuning and with functional discontinuities at the region boundaries. The glomeruli within the same functional region also had similar temporal response dynamics, independent of response amplitude. The chemical property tuning of the regions could be described by region-specific molecular feature sets with region-specific predictive power for the odor responses. Our results suggest a fragmented tuno- and chemotopic organization of the bulb, where glomeruli within the same functional region are tuned to similar chemical properties and are temporally synchronized, which is potentially beneficial for local signal processing.

paper.title: MRI-based prognostic factors and risk stratification for treatment response in post-traumatic olfactory dysfunction.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features associated with treatment response in post-traumatic olfactory dysfunction (PTOD) and to develop an exploratory MRI-based risk score.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 41 patients with PTOD and 41 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Olfactory bulb (OB) volume, morphology, and integrity, olfactory sulcus depth, and structural lesions in olfactory-related cortical regions were assessed on MRI. Olfactory function was evaluated using the Sniffin' Sticks test, and treatment response was defined as an increase of ≥5.5 points in the Threshold-Discrimination-Identification score. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to select MRI features for model development, from which a simplified integer-based scoring system was derived.

RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with PTOD had a shallower left olfactory sulcus and lower proportions of convex OB morphology bilaterally. After a median follow-up of 8 months, 16 of 41 patients (39.0%) met the treatment-response criterion. Three MRI features were retained in the LASSO model: left OB integrity, left orbital gyrus injury, and right temporal lobe injury. The resulting model had an apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.885 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.787-0.983). Full-pipeline internal validation yielded a stratified ten-fold cross-validated AUC of 0.733 (95% CI, 0.564-0.901) and a bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC of 0.725. The simplified three-factor scoring system had an apparent AUC of 0.869 (95% CI, 0.761-0.977) and a bootstrap bias-corrected AUC of 0.867, with treatment response rates of 75.0%, 50.0%, and 5.3% in the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively. The empirical MRI scoring scheme had an apparent AUC of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.662-0.926); the difference between the two scoring systems was not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.079).

CONCLUSION: Baseline structural MRI features were associated with treatment response in PTOD. The exploratory three-factor MRI-based score showed potential for risk stratification within this cohort, but prospective external validation is required before clinical application.

paper.title: Sensory Evaluation of a Receptor-Guided Mixture Designed to Approximate Methyl Eugenol Odor Quality.
paper.abstract: Reconstructing the odor quality of a target compound using alternative aroma ingredients remains a challenge in flavor science and is largely guided by empirical sensory evaluation. As a proof of concept, this study investigated whether human olfactory receptor response patterns can inform candidate selection using methyl eugenol as a model odorant. Functional assays confirmed that methyl eugenol activated OR10G7, OR5K1, and OR2J2, whereas its structural analog, eugenol, predominantly activated OR10G7. To address receptor-response differences between methyl eugenol and eugenol, 2,5-dimethylpyrazine and (E,E)-2,4-decadienal were selected through preliminary sensory evaluation and combined with eugenol to formulate a mixture designed to approximate the target odor quality (Mix). In preliminary exploratory assessments involving six panelists over two sessions, Mix was selected as more similar to methyl eugenol than eugenol in 11 of 12 panelist-session observations in the 2-AFC test; the distance evaluation showed the same directional pattern. Napping and check-all-that-apply (CATA) profiling were descriptively consistent with a directional shift of Mix toward methyl eugenol; notes were not fully reproduced. Dynamic headspace GC-MS analysis showed that eugenol predominated in the DHS-recovered fraction. Collectively, these findings suggest that olfactory receptor response patterns can provide a mechanistically informed basis for narrowing candidate selection, while sensory evaluation can be used to assess whether the resulting mixture perceptually approximates the target odor quality.

paper.title: [Research progress on olfactory bulb MRI for olfactory assessment in patients with Kallmann syndrome].
paper.abstract: Kallmann Syndrome (KS) is a clinical type of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH), which accounts for 40% to 60% of CHH. In addition to gonadal dysfunction, the typical clinical manifestation of KS is olfactory dysfunction. Currently, the clinical assessment of olfaction mainly includes olfactory event-related potentials, the University of Pennsylvania Olfactory Identification Test, the Chinese Olfactory Function Test and the "Smell Stick" identification test 16. The above methods have a large degree of subjectivity, whereas olfactory bulb MRI can determine olfactory function through imaging changes of the olfactory bulb, which has significant clinical value for early olfactory assessment in patients with KS. This article mainly reviews the relevant progress of olfactory bulb MRI in the assessment of olfaction in patients with KS.

paper.title: TBX6-regulated OR51B5 upregulation mediates mitochondrial calcium overload and NLRP3-dependent pyroptosis in imatinib-induced cutaneous adverse reactions.
paper.abstract: Imatinib, a first-line targeted therapy for leukemia and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), frequently induces cutaneous adverse reactions, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identified the ectopic olfactory receptor OR51B5 as a potential mediator of imatinib-induced skin toxicity. OR51B5 expression was markedly upregulated in patients experiencing imatinib-associated skin reactions, as well as in imatinib-treated murine skin tissues and HaCaT keratinocytes. Mechanistically, imatinib activated the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway. Knockdown of OR51B5 attenuated calcium overload and inflammasome activation, whereas its overexpression exacerbated these effects. Further studies identified TBX6 as a direct transcriptional regulator of OR51B5. Molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and ubiquitination analyses demonstrated that imatinib directly interacts with and stabilizes TBX6 by suppressing ubiquitin-mediated degradation, consequently promoting OR51B5 transcription. Upregulation of OR51B5 was associated with cAMP elevation and Ca2+ dysregulation, including mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, leading to ROS accumulation, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Collectively, our findings identify a novel TBX6/OR51B5/calcium/NLRP3 signaling axis underlying imatinib-induced skin toxicity and highlight OR51B5 as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating cutaneous adverse reactions.

paper.title: Dynamic changes in key aroma compounds during the processing of Dangui (Camellia sinensis) tea and the preliminary exploration of its olfactory perception.
paper.abstract: Dangui (Camellia sinensis) is an elite cultivar suitable for processing oolong tea, while the dynamic variation of its volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during processing remains unclear. Here, HS-SPME-GC-MS was performed to explore the dynamic changes in VOCs of Dangui during processing. Results showed that esters transiently accumulated during withering and then declined gradually, while terpenoids generally rose and peaked at rolling with a subsequent slight decrease. Multivariate analysis screened 17 signature VOCs, and 13 of them could form stable complexes with human olfactory receptors. Aroma wheel analysis revealed that dynamic changes in key compounds during tea processing caused continuous increases in the intensities of floral, green, minty and nutty odors. Withering and fermentation primarily regulated nutty, pungent, and woody odors, while rolling and drying dominated the expression of floral, minty, green, and fruity odors. This study clarifies Dangui's unique aroma composition and provides a theoretical foundation for post-processing aroma modulation.

paper.title: Genetic mechanisms underlying feeding behaviour in silkworm larvae.
paper.abstract: The silkworm, an economically important insect that feeds almost exclusively on mulberry leaves, has emerged as a pivotal model for understanding the genetic basis of feeding behaviour in herbivorous specialists. Recent advances have begun to unravel the complex molecular networks that enable efficient host plant recognition, nutrient intake and metabolic adaptation. Feeding behaviour in silkworm larvae is governed by a multi-layered regulatory system that coordinates peripheral detection, internal organ sensing and neuroendocrine regulation. Key players include gustatory and odorant receptors, odorant-binding proteins, odorant-degrading enzymes, neuropeptides and transcription factors, all functioning in a coordinated, tissue-specific manner. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge of these genetic mechanisms within an integrative framework that links peripheral chemosensation and internal organ sensing to neuropeptide regulation and ultimately to behavioural output. We further discuss how comparative and evolutionary perspectives illuminate the genomic and adaptive evolution of mulberry specialization. We also consider emerging regulatory layers, including epigenetic modifications and the microbiota-gut-brain axis, which have been implicated in feeding behaviour in other insects but remain largely unexplored in the silkworm. Finally, we highlight emerging technologies that will advance research in this field, providing a foundation for improving artificial diet-based sericulture.

paper.title: Bitter taste receptors are involved in asthma relieved by aspirin: A hypothesis.
paper.abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) typically do not affect asthma symptoms in most people. However, there are unique subgroups of patients whose responses to NSAIDs diverge considerably from the norm. Among these individuals, some experience an exacerbation of their asthma - commonly identified as aspirin- or NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD and N-ERD, respectively). In contrast, others exhibit a remarkable improvement in their asthma symptoms following the administration of NSAIDs. This improvement is characterized by rapid, pronounced, and long-lasting bronchodilation, resulting in a substantial improvement in clinical symptoms and enhanced respiratory function. The observation of such contrasting responses has prompted further investigation into the mechanisms that might explain this phenomenon. Our hypothesis centers on the activation of bitter taste receptors by NSAIDs, resulting in rapid, significant, and sustained bronchodilation. Notably, this bronchodilator effect closely mirrors the relief observed in those asthma cases that improve with NSAID use. This mechanism provides a potential biological basis for their distinct response to NSAID therapy.

paper.title: M2iOR: a quantitative, context-resolved atlas of insect odorant receptor-odorant interactions.
paper.abstract: Olfactory detection in insects relies on interactions between odorant molecules and odorant receptors (ORs) expressed in olfactory sensory neurons. Although numerous studies have characterized insect OR-ligand interactions, these data remain scattered across the literature and heterogeneous in terms of species, experimental systems, and reporting standards, limiting their systematic analysis. Here, we present the Molecule to Insect Odorant Receptor database (M2iOR, https://m2ior.chemsensim.fr/), a curated, publicly accessible resource designed to centralize and standardize odorant-receptor interaction data. In its current release, M2iOR compiles 35 891 bioassay experiments describing 30 348 distinct insect OR-molecule pairs, extracted from 41 peer-reviewed publications and public databases. The resource integrates ligand structures, receptor sequences, species names, mixture information, and detailed experimental metadata. M2iOR provides flexible query tools allowing users to retrieve activity profiles for individual molecules or compound sets, and identify agonists and nonagonists for specific insect ORs, enabling comparative analyses across receptors, species, or bioassay systems. Advanced filtering based on curated metadata and batch search functionality support high-throughput analyses. For each query, users can visualize and download a curated aggregation of experimental results, including a binarized combinatorial representation of olfactory coding suitable for downstream computational studies. M2iOR provides a comprehensive framework for data-driven research in insect olfaction and comparative chemosensory biology.

paper.title: Individual olfactory channels shape distinct parameters of sleep architecture.
paper.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction and anosmia are associated with disruptions in sleep. In Drosophila melanogaster, broadly inhibiting olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) similarly disrupts sleep. However, due to the diversity of ORNs and the combinatorial nature of olfactory processing, the circuit logic by which ORNs modulate sleep remains unclear. In this study, we paired driver lines of different ensembles of ORNs, individual ORN types, and a known modulator of ORNs with synaptic silencing tools and targeted gene disruptions to further characterize the contributions of ORNs to sleep architecture. We find that the activity of distinct ORN types modulates day and nighttime sleep and heterogeneously shapes parameters of sleep architecture. Furthermore, the effects of ORN signaling on sleep are in part shaped by heterogeneous serotonin (5-HT) receptor expression. Together, this work identifies pathways bridging olfaction and sleep, and establishes a circuit model that can be used to further characterize the behavioral consequences of sensory dysfunction.

paper.title: Cell Wall-Formed Dietary Fiber in Tartary Buckwheat Governs Selective Enrichment of Phytochemicals to Enhanced Postprandial GLP-1 Response.
paper.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is well-known for its biological functions in glucose homeostasis which aligns closely with the antidiabetic function of whole grain foods (WGFs). Here, Tartary buckwheat flour fractions with different particle sizes (small particle size (SF: 0.2 mm), middle particle size (MF: 0.6 mm), and large particle size (BF: 0.9 mm)), reflecting different degrees of cell wall integrity, were used to investigate how particle size modulates GLP-1 secretion. The in vivo mouse study showed that intact endosperm cells from Tartary buckwheat grains significantly increased the postprandial GLP-1 response. Further study demonstrated that only the hydrolysate from BF augmented GLP-1 secretion from enteroendocrine STC-1 L-cells, which is all positively correlated with the selectively enriched phytochemicals in BF particles (ononin, ginkgolide C, pristimerin, and pentadecanoic acid). Significant correlations between particle size, phytochemical profiles and GLP-1 release demonstrated that the integrity of CW-DF is essential to the nutritional properties of WGFs. Molecular docking simulations suggested putative interactions between phytochemicals and bitter taste receptors in GLP-1 secretion. Thus, cell wall integrity is a pivotal regulator of the health benefits of WGFs, offering a mechanistic rationale for minimal processing to harness the health benefits of WGFs through targeted endogenous GLP-1 production.

paper.title: Multi-level insights into the umami perception of Agrocybe aegerita tripeptides: molecular docking, cell signaling, and electroencephalography.
paper.abstract: Umami peptides from Agrocybe aegerita exhibit distinctive umami characteristics, yet systematic studies integrating multiple umami-related receptors with multi-level evidence remain scarce. Molecular docking results suggest that these umami peptides may potentially interact with T1R1/T1R3, CaSR, and GPRC6A, and that different peptide-receptor combinations exhibit certain differences in interaction. In STC-1 cells, the peptides altered receptor mRNA expression and evoked biphasic, concentration-dependent intracellular Ca2+ responses and ATP increases. Electroencephalography showed that the peptides modulated cortical activity mainly in the low-frequency δ band associated with taste processing. DDL produced the strongest and most consistent responses across all assays-plausibly linked to its compact acidic sequence and preferential T1R3 binding. Overall, these findings provide multi-level evidence for the umami activity of A. aegerita peptides and a basis for developing natural flavor enhancers.

paper.title: Learning-associated flexibility of cortical taste coding is impaired in Shank3 knockout mice.
paper.abstract: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning. We found that GC neurons in Shank3 knockout mice exhibited reduced stimulus-evoked suppression and increased trial-to-trial correlated variability during the acquisition of CTA memory. These activity changes, which likely reduced signal-to-noise ratio in GC, were associated with slower CTA acquisition in Shank3 knockout mice. In both genotypes, CTA learning enhanced, while subsequent extinction reduced, taste discriminability in GC, and both extinction and the associated reduction in discriminability were faster in Shank3 knockout than in wild-type mice. Together, these results show that Shank3 loss is associated with destabilized cortical activity dynamics in GC, which may contribute to inefficient encoding and maintenance of learned taste aversion. These findings show that loss of Shank3 compromises the ability of animals to update behavior to incorporate negative outcomes, and suggest this loss of flexibility may be an important feature of monogenic ASDs.

paper.title: Central sodium taste coding in the rostral nucleus of the solitary tract: A hypothesis on sensorimotor transformation.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The taste of sodium is notable among the basic taste modalities because it signals both physiological needs and potential toxicity. Peripheral sodium coding is mediated by distinct epithelial sodium channel (ENaC)-dependent pathways associated with appetitive responses and ENaC-independent pathways associated with aversive behavioral responses. Recent electrophysiological studies indicate that sodium-responsive neuronal populations show partial spatial segregation within the rostral nucleus of the solitary tract (rNST), the first central relay of the gustatory system.

HIGHLIGHT: Evidence reviewed here suggests that amiloride-sensitive and amiloride-insensitive sodium-responsive neurons exhibit partially distinct spatial distributions within the rNST, potentially preserving biologically meaningful categories of sodium stimuli. Because the rNST is strategically positioned within gustatory, somatosensory, autonomic, and feeding-related networks, this organization may support functions extending beyond sensory representation alone. Accordingly, we hypothesize that putative sodium-responsive maps contribute to early sensorimotor transformations by providing differential access to neural circuits underlying ingestion and avoidance.

CONCLUSIONS: Spatially organized sodium-responsive pathways in the rNST may represent an organizational framework that links gustatory coding to feeding-related behavioral control. Further electrophysiological, circuit-tracing, and behavioral studies are required to determine whether sodium taste maps function primarily as sensory representations, as components of sensorimotor circuits, or as integrated systems serving both functions.

paper.title: Microbiome evidence-guided construction of a defined microbial consortium for light-aroma Baijiu fermentation and flavor development.
paper.abstract: Natural fermentation systems harbor microbial resources, but translating microbiome information into cultivable and controllable defined communities remains challenging. We integrated 74 metagenomic datasets from light-aroma Baijiu-associated Daqu and fermented grains with metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) functional profiles and independent 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon time series to propose four candidate functional roles: substrate conversion, acid/acyl-precursor formation, alcoholic fermentation, and aroma formation. Metagenomic profiling revealed community heterogeneity, whereas MAG analysis showed widespread genetic potential for starch conversion and lactic- and acetic-acid-related metabolism. Amplicon data revealed genus-level temporal distributions of Bacillus, Weissella, Wickerhamomyces, and Saccharomyces. Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, Weissella confusa, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Wickerhamomyces anomalus were selected from the available laboratory culture collection as candidate representatives of these roles. A three-factor Box-Behnken design optimized the two bacterial inoculum volumes and the combined yeast volume, with the yeast ratio fixed at 1:1 (v/v). For 500 g of substrate, inoculation volumes were 7 mL for B. amyloliquefaciens, 20 mL for W. confusa, 41 mL for S. cerevisiae, and 41 mL for W. anomalus, yielding 2.28 ± 0.12 g/L ethyl acetate (HPLC). During 28 d of solid-state fermentation, starch, reducing sugars, acidity, and volatile profiles changed, with 51 volatile compounds detected. The final base Baijiu contained 33 volatile compounds, including 13 with odor activity values (OAVs) >1, of which 11 were also detected by gas chromatography-olfactometry (GC-O). These findings support a role-guided route from natural fermentation microbiome evidence to a defined consortium with measurable fermentation and flavor phenotypes.

paper.title: Effects of pre-meal dashi consumption on food preferences and sweet taste sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Impaired sweet taste sensitivity and preferences for energy-dense foods have been reported in patients with type 2 diabetes, although practical strategies to modify these preferences remain limited. We investigated whether consuming dashi, a soup stock rich in umami, before meals could alter food preferences and sweet taste sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: We conducted an open-label randomized controlled trial with an initial 4-week parallel-group period followed by an exploratory 4-week period in which participants received the alternate intervention without a washout interval. Twenty patients with type 2 diabetes were randomly assigned to consume either dashi (dashi group) or hot water (water group) before breakfast and dinner during the initial phase. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the change in sweet taste threshold from baseline to week 4. Secondary outcomes included the feasibility of pre-meal dashi intake, food preferences, biomarkers, anthropometric parameters, and dietary intake. Second-period outcomes were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Eighteen participants (90%) completed the week 4 assessment, and adherence to the dashi intervention was 97%. The adjusted between-group difference in sweet taste threshold was -5.2 g/L (95% CI, -13.1 to 2.9; p = 0.19). In exploratory within-group analyses, preference for non-sweet fatty foods and sweet carbohydrate foods decreased in the dashi group; however, the corresponding adjusted between-group differences were -11 points (95% CI, -28 to 7; p = 0.22) and -8 points (95% CI, -22 to 7; p = 0.29), respectively. Among participants with impaired sweet taste sensitivity at baseline, 3 of 5 (60%) in the dashi group and 0 of 4 (0%) in the water group improved to normal sensitivity (p = 0.17).

CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, pre-meal dashi intake was feasible, but superiority over hot water was not demonstrated. Exploratory findings on food preferences and sweet taste sensitivity are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in further large-scale, independently conducted trials.

paper.title: Familiarity and concentration- based intensity shape spatial patterns of odor-evoked brain activation.
paper.abstract: Olfactory perception is shaped by both the physical properties of odorants and prior odor experience. Odor familiarity and concentration-based perceptual intensity are known to influence neural responses; however, less is known about how odor-evoked brain activation varies across conditions that differ in familiarity and perceived strength. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI, we examined condition-specific activation patterns and brain-behavior relationships during passive odor perception. Sixty-three healthy young women participated in a 2 × 2 factorial fMRI experiment including familiar and unfamiliar odors presented at low- and high-intensity concentrations. Odors were delivered birhinally using a computer-controlled olfactometer, and participants provided in-scanner ratings of perceived odor intensity and odor-evoked memory intensity. Whole-brain analyses were used to describe condition-wise activation maps and direct between-condition contrasts, while region-of-interest analyses focused on canonical olfactory, limbic, and memory-related regions. All odor conditions elicited activation across olfactory, limbic, frontal, parietal, and cerebellar regions. Direct contrasts showed that low-intensity unfamiliar odors elicited greater activation than low-intensity familiar odors in frontal and parietal regions, suggesting increased evaluative processing when weak odor input could not be readily matched to established odor representations. Low-intensity unfamiliar odors also elicited greater activation than high-intensity unfamiliar odors in precuneus and supramarginal/angular regions. Brain-behavior analyses showed significant associations only for familiar odors presented at low intensity, where subjective memory intensity was negatively correlated with bilateral parahippocampal activation. These findings suggest that odor familiarity and concentration-based intensity contribute to condition-specific patterns of odor-evoked brain activation, with low-intensity familiar odors revealing a selective relationship between odor-evoked memory experience and medial temporal responses.

paper.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
paper.abstract: Hypertension, the leading modifiable risk factor for global mortality, is driven in >50% of cases by neurogenic mechanisms linked to heightened sympathetic nerve activity (SNA). A hallmark of neurogenic hypertension is the exacerbation of respiratory-modulated SNA (RespSNA) and resulting blood pressure Traube-Hering (TH) waves, which emerges during the prehypertensive period and contributes to disease development. Carotid bodies (CBs), the peripheral chemoreceptors involved in the hypoxic response, are hyperactive in hypertensive patients and animal models. Their chronic intermittent stimulation, as seen in obstructive sleep apnoea, promotes hypertension characterised by exacerbated RespSNA and TH waves. Yet, their causal role in initiating these changes remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether acute intermittent CB stimulations could directly enhance RespSNA, TH waves and blood pressure from a physiological baseline, using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats. Four brief CB stimulations with sodium cyanide, mimicking acute intermittent hypoxia, were sufficient to induce a prolonged (>20 min) increase in both inspiratory and late expiratory RespSNA bursts, TH waves and perfusion pressure, with these effects being prevented by carotid sinus denervation. These changes were accompanied by a reconfiguration of central respiratory and cardiovascular control, including elevated respiratory heart rate variability and enhanced respiratory drive targeting upper airway and abdominal muscles. Our findings demonstrate that acute intermittent CB activation triggers sustained RespSNA and elevation of TH waves, supporting its potential role in development of hypertension. Our data also suggest that CBs play a key role in initiating this respiratory-cardiovascular plasticity and that central mechanisms might contribute to its long-term maintenance. KEY POINTS: Carotid body (CB) overactivity is implicated in sympathetic excitation and development of hypertension, but its direct role in initiating respiratory-cardiovascular dysfunction remains unresolved. We tested whether brief, repeated CB stimulations could trigger lasting changes in breathing and blood pressure control from a physiological baseline. In rats, only four stimulations induced a persistent increase in respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, elevating blood pressure fluctuations (Traube-Hering waves) and mean blood pressure. These effects, prevented by carotid sinus denervation, were linked to enhanced respiratory-cardiovascular coupling and altered upper airway and abdominal motor control. Our findings reveal that short-term CB activation can induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling, relevant to both physiological adaptations and hypertension pathogenesis.

paper.title: Ectopic olfactory neuroblastoma - complete response to chemotherapy following a late recurrence: A case report.
paper.abstract: Olfactory neuroblastoma, also known as esthesioneuroblastoma, is a rare type of cancer that originates in the nerve tissue of the olfactory epithelium, located in the upper part of the nasal cavity. The present study reports the case of a female patient who was 35 years old at the time of diagnosis in 2013, with an ectopic olfactory neuroblastoma (Hyams grade III, Kadish stage B) in the right sphenoid sinus, associated with the paraneoplastic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH). Following transnasal endoscopic surgical resection and adjuvant intensity-modulated radiotherapy (60 Gy) in 2014, the SIADH resolved and the patient achieved complete remission. After a 10-year latency period, in April 2024 the patient developed a late, destructive local recurrence (5.3×4.7 cm) with extension to the maxillary sinus and right orbit. Given the technical limitations for salvage surgery and the refusal of re-irradiation, a multidisciplinary committee approved the administration of 6 cycles of systemic chemotherapy with cisplatin (75 mg/m2) and etoposide (100 mg/m2) every 21 days. Treatment began in June 2024 and concluded in September 2024. Treatment was well tolerated, with only grade 1 nausea and transient grade 2 myelosuppression. Close follow-up with contrast-enhanced head and neck CT in December 2025 confirmed the complete clinical and radiological response, demonstrating the total absence of the tumor lesion. As of February 2026, the patient remains asymptomatic and disease-free. The present case highlights the rarity of ectopic sphenoid location, the usefulness of SIADH as an indirect biomarker and the high chemosensitivity of high-grade variants in late recurrences, justifying prolonged and indefinite follow-up.

paper.title: Olfactory deficits and structural anomalies of the peripheral olfactory system in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 25% of individuals with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DS) develop a psychotic disorder, and the syndrome shares key neurodevelopmental features with psychosis in the general population. The olfactory system develops early in utero, providing a window into gestational disruptions relevant to psychosis risk. We hypothesized that 22q11DS would show impairments in olfactory function and structural anomalies of the olfactory system relative to psychosis spectrum (PS) youth without a known genetic syndrome and typically developing controls (TD).

METHODS: Participants included individuals with 22q11DS (n = 101), PS (n = 56), and TD (n = 52). Sinonasal symptoms, odor identification, and discrimination (Sniffin' Sticks) behaviorally. Structural 3 T MRI measured olfactory bulb volume, sulcus depth, and sulcus length. Sample sizes vary per analysis.

RESULTS: Relative to TD, 22q11DS showed elevated sinonasal burden (p < .001), lower odor identification (p < .001), and lower odor discrimination (p < .001). PS showed elevated sinonasal burden (p < .001) and marginally lower odor identification (p = .06), but no discrimination deficit. Olfactory bulb volume was significantly smaller in 22q11DS versus TD (p = .007, r = 0.39); PS showed a non-significant trend (p = .07). Olfactory sulcus depth (p = .52) and length (p = .82) did not differ across groups.

CONCLUSIONS: 22q11DS is associated with elevated sinonasal burden, robust olfactory identification and discrimination deficits exceeding those of PS and reduced olfactory bulb volume. The co-occurrence of functional deficits and reduced bulb volume without sulcal anomalies may distinguish the 22q11DS olfactory phenotype from that of PS. These hypothesis-generating findings are consistent with partially dissociable neurodevelopmental mechanisms and support the utility of 22q11DS as a genetic model for psychosis risk.

paper.title: Limited Long-Range Olfactory Discrimination in a MATOPIBA Lineage of Encarsia (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae) Across Resistant and Susceptible Crop Cultivars.
paper.abstract: Herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) are key mediators of tritrophic interactions, frequently guiding parasitoid host-searching behaviour over long distances. However, the reliability and discriminatory power of these cues may depend on plant resistance traits and herbivore identity. Here, we evaluated whether volatile emissions from resistant and susceptible soybean and common bean cultivars infested by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci MEAM1 or the aphid Aphis craccivora influence the long-range foraging responses of an undescribed Encarsia lineage from the MATOPIBA region (Brazil). Using Y-tube olfactometer bioassays, we recorded initial choice and residence time of individual females exposed to contrasting plant-herbivore combinations. Choice frequencies were analyzed using chi-square tests, and residence time using non-parametric analyses, including paired comparisons between olfactometer arms within each contrast. Across all contrasts, parasitoids showed no significant discrimination between resistant and susceptible cultivars, between host plant species, or between plants infested by different herbivores. Residence time did not differ among treatments or between arms within contrasts. These results suggest that, under the experimental conditions tested (plant-vs.-plant contrasts without a positive control), volatile blends emitted by these crop systems did not provide sufficiently contrasting long-range cues to influence parasitoid orientation. The observed behavioural pattern is consistent with a generalist long-range foraging strategy in which host location may depend more strongly on short-range or contact-mediated signals. Our findings highlight context-dependent limits of volatile-mediated signalling in agroecosystems and contribute to understanding how plant resistance and herbivore identity interact with parasitoid sensory ecology.

paper.title: Individual variation in food odor sensitivity is related to neuropeptide signaling and starvation in Drosophila.
paper.abstract: Olfaction is fundamental for animal survival, and individual variation exists in olfactory sensitivity. However, the underlying mechanisms of such variations remain unclear. paper.title: Chemical composition and odor intensity of plant volatile organic compounds drive medicinal use.
paper.abstract: Sensory cues like taste and smell are assumed to influence medicinal plant selection. However, the precise role of odor intensity and chemical properties awaits experimental investigation. This study investigated the correlation between Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) and medicinal plant selection by a local community in NE-Brazil. We conducted semi-structured interviews to identify the main plant species used within the local medical system, as well as the participants' subjective perception about the odor intensity of medicinal plants. Subsequently, we collected VOCs samples from 39 ethnospecies using dynamic headspace methods and analyzed them through gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry. We then tested how odor perception influences the type and number of body systems a plant treats, and how VOC emission and composition affect plant odor perception and use. Among these frequently cited, odorous medicinal plants, olfactory perception was significantly associated with a plant's citation frequency for therapeutic uses, irrespective of the associated body system. Odor intensity correlates with total VOC emission and chemical diversity, with monoterpenes specifically enhancing perceived fragrance. Furthermore, plants sharing similar VOC compositions or chemical classes often treat related body systems. These findings reveal a sensory-chemical logic in local medical systems, pointing to a critical importance of odor perception and chemical composition in the selection and use of medicinal plants, and advocating for expanded interdisciplinary research in this field.

Criterion-related validity was assessed using a hospital meal preference survey, and concurrent validity was examined in a Nutrition Support Team cohort (n=53).

paper.title: Salivary Carbonic Anhydrase VI and Gustatory Function Among Adults Assessed After Orthognathic Surgery: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
paper.abstract: Background/Objectives: Biological determinants of interindividual variation in gustatory function following orthognathic surgery remain poorly understood. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 100 adults following orthognathic surgery at three centers. Unstimulated salivary CA VI concentration and flow rate were measured under standardized conditions. Separate proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression models assessed associations between CA VI and each taste threshold, adjusting for age, sex, smoking status, salivary flow rate, postoperative interval, and surgical territory. paper.title: Relating olfaction-related quality of life and psychophysical olfactory performance: validation of the Hebrew questionnaire of olfactory disorders.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Olfactory dysfunction substantially affects olfaction-related quality of life, daily functioning, safety, and well-being, yet a validated, comprehensive, Hebrew, olfaction-specific patient-reported outcome measure is unavailable.

OBJECTIVES: To translate, culturally adapt, and validate the Hebrew version of the Questionnaire of Olfactory Disorders (He-QOD).

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 90 patients with OD and 48 healthy controls. Participants completed the He-QOD, Sniffin' Sticks threshold-discrimination-identification (TDI) testing, and a Hebrew-adapted University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT). Thirty-three participants underwent retesting after at least 4 weeks. Internal consistency, test-retest reliability, known-group validity, convergent validity, and discriminative ability were evaluated.

RESULTS: The total He-QOD had excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.931) and test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.971). Patients had higher total and domain scores than controls (all p < 0.001). Total He-QOD score correlated inversely with TDI (ρ = -0.57, p < 0.001) and UPSIT scores (ρ = -0.56, p < 0.001). Areas under receiver operating characteristic curves ranged from 0.833 to 0.846.

CONCLUSION: The He-QOD is a reliable and valid tool for assessing the patient-reported burden of OD among Hebrew-speaking populations. Its association with two psychophysical assessments supports its use alongside objective testing in clinical and research settings.

paper.title: Olfactory network variability is associated with odor identification and cognitive performance in mild cognitive impairment.
paper.abstract: BackgroundOdor identification impairment is an early marker of Alzheimer's disease pathology and predicts dementia conversion in mild cognitive impairment (MCI). However, the pathophysiological role of dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) variability within olfactory networks remains unclear.ObjectiveTo characterize seed-based dFC variability across olfactory pathways in MCI with odor identification impairment (MCI-OII) and examine its associations with olfactory and cognitive performance.MethodsNinety-seven patients with MCI were recruited and subdivided into MCI-OII and those without odor identification impairment (MCI-NOII), along with 97 age-matched healthy controls (HC). All participants underwent neuropsychological assessment, olfactory testing, and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Seed-based dFC variability was computed using a sliding window approach. Correlation and exploratory mediation analyses examined associations among abnormal dFC, odor identification, and cognition.ResultsCompared to MCI-NOII and HC, MCI-OII exhibited increased dFC variability between the left piriform cortex/right insula and right caudate nucleus, and between the left insula and left middle frontal gyrus. For the connection between the left insula and left cerebellar lobule VI, dFC variability showed a graded pattern from MCI-OII to HC to MCI-NOII. Increased caudate-centered dFC variability was associated with poorer odor identification, memory, and executive performance. Furthermore, exploratory mediation analyses suggested indirect associations involving odor identification, caudate-centered dFC variability, and memory or executive function.ConclusionsMCI-OII is characterized by increased olfactory-network dFC variability, particularly in caudate-centered pathways. These findings suggest that dFC variability may serve as a candidate network-level marker of concurrent olfactory impairment and cognitive dysfunction in MCI.

paper.title: Inter-nostril olfactory asymmetry in nasal septal deviation: a controlled cross-sectional study.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nasal septal deviation may be associated with side-specific differences in olfactory performance. This study aimed to compare side-specific olfactory function and absolute inter-nostril asymmetry between people with nasal septal deviation and healthy controls and to evaluate the association between the severity of global subjective nasal obstruction and directional olfactory asymmetry.

METHODS: A prospective single-center controlled cross-sectional study was conducted, including 61 patients with nasal septal deviation and 48 controls comparable in age and sex. Side-specific TDI scores (Sniffin' Sticks threshold, discrimination, and identification tests) for each nasal cavity were collected. The absolute inter-nostril asymmetry (|ΔTDI|) was calculated based on the side-to-side difference in TDI scores. Subjective nasal obstruction was assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS).

RESULTS: Composite TDI scores of patients with septal deviation were significantly lower on the deviated side than on the wider side (26.81 ± 5.49 vs. 31.77 ± 3.36, respectively; mean difference, 4.96 points; 95% confidence interval, 3.34-6.58; p < 0.001), whereas no significant side-to-side difference was found in controls (p = 0.236). Absolute inter-nostril asymmetry was significantly higher in patients than in controls (median [interquartile range] = 6.00 [2.25-9.50] vs. 2.13 [0.75-3.81]; p < 0.001). The correlation between the VAS score and directional olfactory asymmetry was positive in patients (Spearman's ρ = 0.561; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: People with nasal septal deviation demonstrated decreased TDI scores on the deviated side and increased absolute inter-nostril asymmetry compared to controls. The clinical implications of these findings require further study.

paper.title: The nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract is required for learning odor-guided food avoidance.
paper.abstract: Foraging animals must continually evaluate whether potential food sources are safe to consume. Such decisions rely on both innate preferences and learned associations formed through prior experience. Consumption of a food followed by malaise or sickness leads to avoidance of that food, reflecting learned associations between sensory cues that identify a food and its negative post-ingestive consequences. Although this form of learning has been studied extensively using taste cues, taste signals arise only after oral contact, at which point exposure to potential toxins has already occurred. Olfactory cues, in contrast, provide information about potential food sources prior to consumption, yet how odors acquire aversive value remains unclear. Here, using targeted chemogenetic perturbations, we identify the nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract (NLOT), which has direct bidirectional connectivity to olfactory regions and the basolateral amygdala, as a critical circuit element for odor-aversion learning in male and female mice. We find that the NLOT is required for conditioned odor aversion but is dispensable for other odor-guided behaviors and for fear conditioning driven by a non-olfactory cue. Our findings identify a selective role for the NLOT in linking olfactory cues to learned aversive outcomes, that supports odor-guided behavioral decisions.Significance statement Animals rely on smell to evaluate food safety before consuming it, yet the brain circuits that link odor cues to learned aversive outcomes remain poorly understood. Here we identify the nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract (NLOT), a largely unstudied region at the interface between olfactory and limbic circuits, as a critical and selective node for conditioned odor aversion learning. Chemogenetic perturbations of the NLOT disrupted both the acquisition and expression of odor-malaise associations, while leaving odor detection, odor discrimination, and non-olfactory fear learning intact - revealing a previously unrecognized specialization within olfactory-amygdala circuits that supports odor-guided decisions about food safety.

paper.title: [Research Progress on the Use of Canine Olfaction for Bloodstain Evidence Search].

paper.title: Functional characterization of the pheromone receptor OR67d within the genus Drosophila.
paper.abstract: Insects rely on chemosensory cues to mediate essential behaviors, including mate recognition. In Drosophila melanogaster, the odorant receptor OR67d detects the male-specific pheromone cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA), initiating diverse behavioral responses. Here, we characterize OR67d receptors from nine Drosophila species using phylogenetic analysis, transgenic expression, and electrophysiology. While most orthologs retained sensitivity to cVA, some exhibited broader tuning, responding to structurally similar acetates. Notably, D. bipectinata and D. navojoa responded to cVA despite not producing it, raising the possibility that cVA detection has been maintained independently of endogenous production, possibly as a heterospecific cue. Structural modeling revealed overall high sequence conservation yet identified variable regions within the putative binding pocket potentially underlying differences in ligand selectivity. These findings contribute to our understanding of pheromone receptor evolution and how chemical communication systems diversify across Drosophila species.

paper.title: Receptor Allosterism Governs the Coding of Configurational Walnut Aroma.
paper.abstract: Walnut aroma is a configurational odor identity, primarily attributed to a walnut-typical 1:1 concentration ratio of the key food odorants (KFO) (2E,4E,6Z)-nona-2,4,6-trienal and 3-hydroxy-4,5-dimethylfuran-2(5H)-one (sotolon), which by themselves impart oatmeal- and fenugreek-like odor notes, respectively. paper.title: Breed-Associated Roasted Aroma Signatures Across Eight Chinese Sheep Breeds: Integrating Fatty Acid Composition, Volatile Profiles, and Aroma-Active Compounds.

paper.title: Taste testing: gustometry deciphered - a scoping review.
paper.abstract:
PURPOSE: To map and synthesize the protocols and methodological approaches used in chemical gustometry with taste solutions, focusing on taste assessment methods, the solutions and substances employed, concentration ranges and units of measurement, and the procedures used to determine taste thresholds.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework.

RESULTS: Of 6,881 records identified, 10 studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising 722 participants across three clinical contexts (oncology/hematology, diabetes mellitus, and otologic disease). The whole-mouth sip-and-spit method and assessment of detection/recognition thresholds were most frequently used. Substantial heterogeneity in methods, tastants, and concentration units limited comparability across studies.

CONCLUSION: Standardization of chemical gustometry protocols remains a challenge given the methodological heterogeneity identified, underscoring the need for greater methodological rigor and consistency in future research to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability.

paper.title: Identification and Virtual Screening of Umami Peptides in HPLC Fractions of Tauco by LC-MS/MS and Bioinformatics Tools.
paper.abstract: Tauco is a traditional Indonesian fermented soybean product with a characteristic umami flavor mainly attributed to the free amino acids and peptides produced during fermentation. Screened peptides were analyzed for peptide profiles using ToxinPred for toxicity predictions, AllerTop for allergenicity predictions, and ProtParam for GRAVY Score and Instability Index predictions. Furthermore, this study highlights the potential of integrated peptidomics and computational approaches for the discovery of umami peptides from fermented foods. These findings establish a scientific foundation for future research and application of umami peptides in umami ingredients.

paper.title: Genetic variation in behavioral and physiological responses to copper in Drosophila melanogaster.
paper.abstract: Anthropogenic copper (Cu) contamination from agriculture, mining, and industrial runoff creates environmental gradients affecting physiology and behavior in wild populations. All three traits showed substantial phenotypic variation among RILs. Feeding and oviposition avoidance were both highly heritable (H² ∼ 0.88), and RIL identity accounted for 49.5% of the variance in LT50. However, the three traits showed no significant correlation across RILs, suggesting distinct genetic architectures. We identified a single male specific quantitative trait locus (QTL) on chromosome 2R that explained 17.7% of the variation in feeding preference. The interval included candidate detoxification genes Jheh1, Jheh2, Jheh3 and sano, the latter of which is associated with olfactory behavior. No significant QTL were detected for oviposition preference, suggesting a highly polygenic structure that may be difficult to detect with our limited panel size. Together, these results indicate that Cu resistance in D. melanogaster is genetically modular. Behavioral avoidance during feeding, oviposition, and physiological tolerance are heritable but architecturally distinct components, each with potential to respond to selection independently.

paper.title: Neuronal AIMP2-α-synuclein synergy drives endogenous tau and amyloid-β pathologies and neurodegeneration in a mechanistic model of Lewy body dementia.
paper.abstract: Lewy body dementia (LBD), encompassing Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), is defined by widespread α-synuclein (αSyn) aggregation and frequently exhibits coexistent tau and amyloid-β (Aβ) pathologies. However, whether αSyn pathology is sufficient to drive endogenous tau and Aβ aggregation has remained unclear due to a lack of in vivo models that recapitulate the full spectrum of LBD-associated proteinopathies and neurodegeneration. AIMP2, a parkin substrate that accumulates in Parkinson's disease, enhances αSyn aggregation and toxicity, but its role in initiating downstream mixed pathologies across vulnerable brain regions has not been demonstrated in vivo. Here, we generated a conditional, neuron-specific Tet-Off double-transgenic mouse model enabling post-developmental coexpression of AIMP2 and A53T αSyn. This synergistic coexpression induced rapid and widespread αSyn aggregation, detergent-insoluble Lewy-like inclusions, mitochondrial degeneration, synaptic impairment, and neuronal loss, accompanied by marked gliosis. Mice developed key clinical features of LBD, including progressive cognitive impairment, bradykinesia, and olfactory deficits. Notably, without tau or APP overexpression, endogenous tau became hyperphosphorylated through dysregulated kinase signaling, and Aβ accumulated predominantly as TBS-soluble Aβ42 monomers/oligomers without fibrillar plaque deposition, demonstrating that AIMP2-αSyn-driven pathology is sufficient to trigger downstream tauopathy and Aβ pathologies. These mixed pathologies were associated with lysosomal and proteasomal dysfunction, evidenced by p62 and polyubiquitinated protein accumulation. Proteomic analysis identified dysregulation of pathways linked to amyloid processing, synaptic trafficking, and protein quality control. Importantly, temporal suppression of AIMP2 and αSyn expression promoted reduction of pre-existing pathologies and partially restored cognitive function. This study establishes a genetically controlled in vivo model of LBD-like mixed proteinopathy recapitulating αSyn aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, Aβ accumulation, neurodegeneration, and behavioral decline. These findings support a mechanistic link between AIMP2-enhanced αSyn toxicity and secondary proteinopathies and position this model as a platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies in complex α-synucleinopathies.

paper.title: Intranasal Pathogenesis-Adaptive Nanotherapeutics Reinstate Regenerative Competence for Post-Stroke Neural Repair.
paper.abstract: Poststroke neurorehabilitation is limited by the poor regenerative capacity of adult neurons. Although neural stem cells (NSCs) can generate new neurons, their reparative potential is constrained by inefficient delivery to cerebral lesions and a hostile regenerative niche. Here, analysis of a single-nucleus transcriptomic dataset revealed pronounced dysfunction and intercellular crosstalk among neurons, microglia, and NSCs, highlighting redox imbalance and impaired nitric oxide (NO) signaling as potential therapeutic targets. Guided by these findings, we develop FCeO2@GLp, a pathogenesis-adaptive nanotherapeutic integrating reactive oxygen species scavenging, NO replenishment and immune modulation within cerebral ischemic microenvironment. Following intranasal administration, FCeO2@GLp actively adheres to the olfactory epithelium (OE), reaches infarcted brain regions, releases cerium oxide (CeO2) nanozyme, fingolimod, and a NO donor in response to local acidity. This coordinated strategy alleviates oxidative stress, reprograms microglia, protects neurons, and enhances NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation. Consequently, FCeO2@GLp effectively reduces infarct volume and cerebral edema during the acute phase, and improves long-term neurological function and survival, establishing a lesion-responsive strategy for poststroke neural repair.

paper.title: Functional aspects of cerebrospinal fluid drainage through the cribriform plate.
paper.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) clearance is essential for maintaining brain homeostasis, yet the contribution of the nasal efflux pathway remains incompletely understood. Here, we combined dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, optical imaging, and anatomical studies across mice and pigs to characterize the dynamics, regulation, and conservation of nasal CSF drainage. We found that CSF rapidly exited the brain via the cribriform plate, especially during acute volume shifts, and that this route slowed down in aged mice when a small-molecular-weight tracer was used. By contrast, olfactory sensory neuron ablation and amyloid beta1-42 exposure impaired uptake of CSF into the nasal pathway. Notably, signal uptake in superficial cervical lymph nodes appeared distinct from meningeal lymphatic drainage, suggesting functional specialization. Our corroborating findings in pigs further solidify the nasal CSF efflux route as a dynamic, evolutionarily conserved, and potentially targetable pathway with relevance to neuroimmune interactions, aging, and neurodegeneration.

paper.title: Evidence generation for diabetes prevention and treatment through the integration of clinical medicine, nutritional epidemiology, and behavioral science.
paper.abstract: Diet and other lifestyle factors are central to diabetes prevention and management. Effective dietary and lifestyle support requires consideration of differences in pathophysiology, food culture, and living circumstances. This narrative review summarizes our research integrating clinical medicine, nutritional epidemiology, and behavioral science, with a particular focus on diet quality. Analyses of large US cohorts showed that higher-quality plant-based diets were associated with lower risks of stroke and mortality. In longitudinal biomarker analyses, increases in healthful plant-based diet scores were associated with favorable changes in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, whereas increases in unhealthful plant-based diet scores were associated with unfavorable changes in inflammatory biomarkers. Metabolite profiles related to healthful plant-based diets were also associated with lower type 2 diabetes risk. Building on earlier work on adiponectin and type 1 diabetes, our studies in Japan showed that even small weight changes were associated with type 2 diabetes risk, depending on age and baseline body mass index. Visceral fat correlated with ectopic fat, and fast eating and eating late at night were associated with greater pancreatic fat deposition. In older adults, lower sweet taste sensitivity was associated with frailty and poorer mental health-related quality of life. These findings suggest that diet quality and lifestyle should be assessed together with each person's metabolic characteristics and living circumstances. Intervention and implementation studies based on this largely observational evidence are the next step toward individualized diabetes prevention and care.
