paper.title: A Curcumin-Based Polyherbal Slow-Dissolving Buccal Lozenge (CBFP-ODS) and Changes in Gingival Inflammation, Plaque Accumulation, Bleeding on Probing and Oral Malodour: A 12-Week Prospective Single-Arm Interventional Study in Young Adults.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plaque-induced gingivitis is the most prevalent reversible inflammatory condition of the gingival tissues and remains under-managed at the population level. Chlorhexidine, the most extensively studied chemical adjunct, is limited in sustained daily use by staining, taste alteration and mucosal effects, which motivates interest in botanically based oral wellness adjuncts intended for everyday use. This study was an uncontrolled, exploratory, hypothesis-generating evaluation of one such adjunct.

METHODS: We evaluated a curcumin-based functional phytotherapeutic oral delivery system (CBFP-ODS), a sugar-free, slow-dissolving buccal lozenge containing six standardised botanicals (Curcuma longa, Ocimum sanctum, Zingiber officinale, Cinnamomum verum, Mentha piperita and Piper longum), in adults aged 18-35 years with mild-to-moderate gingivitis. In a prospective, single-arm, open-label, pre- and post-interventional study (120 enrolled), participants used one lozenge twice daily for 12 weeks while continuing routine mechanical plaque control. Outcomes at five timepoints (baseline, 1 week, 21 days, 45 days, 12 weeks) included the modified gingival index (MGI; primary outcome), the Silness and Löe Plaque Index (PI), the Ainamo and Bay Bleeding on Probing (BOP) index, an examiner-rated organoleptic score, an adapted breath-related self-perception (BRSP) scale and a WHO-adapted oral hygiene and behaviour composite. The pre-specified primary analysis was a completer analysis of the 115 participants with complete follow-up; a mixed-effects model on all 120 enrolled participants was the sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: In the primary completer analysis (n = 115), MGI decreased from 1.78 (SD 0.41) to 0.96 (SD 0.36) (mean change 0.82, 95% CI: 0.73-0.91; t (114) = 18.9; p < 0.001; Cohen's dz ~1.76). Plaque, BOP, oral malodour and self-perceived breath showed within-subject reductions of ~43%-53%, and the behavioural composite increased by ~31% (all p < 0.001). The mixed-effects sensitivity analysis on all 120 enrolled participants gave a concordant estimated reduction of 0.81 MGI units (95% CI: 0.73-0.89). No product-related adverse events were recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-arm study, twice-daily use of CBFP-ODS was associated with within-subject improvements in gingival, plaque, bleeding and breath-related outcomes over 12 weeks. Because the design was uncontrolled and open-label, these observations cannot separate the effect of the intervention from improved oral hygiene behaviour, participation effects, regression to the mean or natural clinical variation and are hypothesis-generating. They do not demonstrate efficacy or verify mucosal absorption. Randomised, placebo-controlled and active-controlled trials are required before any statement about efficacy can be made. Trial Registration: Clinical Trials Registry, India: (CTRI/2025/06/088964; prospectively registered).

paper.title: Parental Bonding and the Recognition and Preference for One's Own Child's Body Odour.
paper.abstract: Previous research has shown that parents can recognise and positively evaluate their infant's odour, but the extent to which these processes relate to individual differences in bonding remains unclear. Addressing this gap, we examined whether parent-reported bonding difficulties are associated with odour recognition accuracy and hedonic evaluation of a child's body odour. A sample of 86 parent-child dyads (children aged 3 months to 3 years) participated in a body odour assessment paradigm. Bonding was measured using the Postpartum Bonding Questionnaire (PBQ). Odour identification involved selecting the child's odour from six samples, including the child's own odour, four odours from other children and a blank sample. Pleasantness was rated for each sample on a visual analogue scale ranging from 0 to 100. Logistic and linear regression analyses were conducted, controlling for parent sex, parent age and child age. Higher PBQ scores, indicating greater parent-reported bonding difficulties, were associated with a higher likelihood of correctly identifying the child's odour, and this effect remained significant after controlling for other covariates. In contrast, bonding difficulties were not associated with the child's body odour pleasantness ratings. These findings suggest that parental olfactory processing comprises at least two partially dissociable components: offspring recognition and hedonic evaluation, which may serve distinct functions in parent-child relationships.

paper.title: The Serum Proteomic Signatures Associated With Organ Dysfunction Based on Phoenix Criteria in Pediatric Sepsis: A Pilot Study.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the serum proteomic characteristics linked to sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, as defined by the Phoenix Pediatric Sepsis (PPS) criteria.

DESIGN AND SETTING: We conducted a serum proteomic study using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry in pediatric patients with sepsis, admitted to the PICU at a tertiary, university-affiliated children's hospital in China.

PATIENTS: Thirty-eight patients with sepsis and 19 healthy controls were included from November 2020 to June 2022.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 403 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified in the serum of pediatric sepsis patients compared with healthy controls. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis revealed that DEPs across the four PPS-defined organ dysfunction were enriched in the antimicrobial humoral response, negative regulation of inflammation, plasminogen activation, and cytokine-mediated signaling pathways. Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) showed that the MEgreen module was highly associated with the PPS score and was enriched in neutrophils. Further analysis identified seven hub proteins (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1 [TIMP1], cathepsin L peptidase 1, β-1,4-galactosyltransferase 1, carbonic anhydrase 3, interleukin 1 receptor like 1, olfactomedin 4, and cathepsin G [CATG]) as candidate serum proteomic markers of organ dysfunction risk. We used the expression of these seven hub proteins in a least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression model to predict organ system dysfunction. It achieved an area under the curve of 0.857 for the coagulation system and 0.769 for the cardiovascular system. All seven hub proteins were significantly correlated with lactic acid and the international normalized ratio (all p < 0.05); CATG was positively correlated with mean arterial pressure (p = 0.005), TIMP1 displayed a positive correlation with d-dimer (p = 0.021) and a negative correlation with platelet (p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: We identified seven hub proteins that constitute a novel proteomic signature for predicting sepsis-associated organ dysfunction based on the Phoenix criteria. It is particularly relevant to the coagulation and cardiovascular systems.

paper.title: Molecular Basis of Bitterness Modulation during Black Tea Fermentation.
paper.abstract: Black tea fermentation involves enzymatic oxidation of catechins into characteristic phenolics such as theaflavins and thearubigins, which profoundly influence bitterness perception. However, the molecular mechanisms by which progressive phenolic oxidation modulates bitterness remain incompletely understood. In this study, controlled oxidation model systems were investigated using an integrated strategy combining cell-based calcium imaging, molecular simulations, and AFM-based single-molecule force measurements. Cell-based assays showed that tyrosinase-mediated oxidation enhanced TAS2R14 activation, whereas endogenous enzyme and laccase mediated oxidation markedly reduced intracellular calcium responses. Molecular simulations revealed that theaflavins exhibit higher binding stability, lower binding free energy, and stronger activation-related conformational effects on TAS2R14 than catechins. Consistently, AFM measurements confirmed stronger adhesion forces for theaflavin-TAS2R14 interactions. In contrast, further oxidative dimerization imposed steric constraints that weakened receptor binding and activation. Collectively, this study clarifies how progressive phenolic oxidation during tea fermentation differentially modulates bitterness at the molecular and receptor levels.

paper.title: Fluoroscopy-Guided Combined Intradiscal and Transforaminal Ventral Epidural Injection Containing Botulinum Toxin Type A and Steroid for Suspected Discogenic Low Back Pain: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence for multi-agent intradiscal and epidural injection in suspected discogenic low back pain is limited. We evaluated a mixture of botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A), lidocaine, triamcinolone, and dextrose.

METHODS: Adults undergoing the combined procedure were reviewed retrospectively. Under fluoroscopy, a transforaminal approach through Kambin's triangle permitted intradiscal injection followed by needle withdrawal for contrast-confirmed ventral epidural injection through the same corridor. Visual analog scale (VAS) scores were assessed at baseline, one week, one month, and three months. Paired comparisons accounted for repeated procedures within patients. Responder thresholds were reductions of at least 2 points, 30%, or 50%. Missing three-month outcomes were classified as nonresponse in a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: The analysis comprised 113 procedures in 88 patients. Follow-up VAS was available for 106, 87, and 73 procedures. Mean VAS decreased from 7.9 to 3.7, 3.8, and 4.3; the three-month paired reduction was 3.6 points (95% CI, 2.7-4.5; P < 0.001). At three months, 45/73 procedures (62%) achieved at least 30% improvement; the missing-as-nonresponse estimate was 45/113 (40%). Among 34 procedures with an early score before loss to three-month follow-up, 22 (65%) had at least 30% improvement. Two adverse events occurred among 115 safety-reviewed procedures (1.7%): transient bilateral leg weakness requiring hospitalization and self-limited dysgeusia.

CONCLUSIONS: This four-agent, dual-site protocol showed a preliminary short-term pain-response signal. The uncontrolled design cannot isolate a BoNT-A effect or confirm the proposed neural mechanisms. Prospective controlled evaluation and safety monitoring are required.

paper.title: Analysis of Invasion Patterns in Occult Involvement Cases of Olfactory Neuroblastoma Using Anatomically Oriented Surgical Specimens.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurate preoperative evaluation of tumor extension in olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) is critical for optimizing surgical planning, particularly for predicting unexpected intracranial and contralateral invasion. However, discrepancies between preoperative imaging and postoperative pathology remain a challenge. This study compares preoperative imaging with detailed pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented specimens to assess ONB progression, characterize patterns associated with unexpected invasion, and improve surgical strategies.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 58 ONB patients who underwent endoscopic transnasal resection at Jikei University Hospital between January 2018 and March 2024. Preoperative computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging were reviewed by a radiology specialist and compared with postoperative pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented resected specimens. Tumors were classified using Kadish staging and Hyams grading.

RESULTS: The cohort had a median age of 53 years (range, 29-85 years), with 67.2% male participants. Preoperative staging classified 37.9% of the cases as Kadish C. Among 36 cases preoperatively staged as Kadish A or B, eight (22.2%) exhibited occult intracranial involvement. Unexpected contralateral invasion was observed in five cases, all Kadish C, frequently associated with tumor progression through bony transition areas at the skull base and nasal septum junction. Tumor invasion into the crista galli was identified in six cases, with one case suggesting metastatic spread rather than direct invasion.

CONCLUSIONS: Occult intracranial involvement in Kadish A and B cases may warrant consideration of skull base resection even in early stages. Contralateral invasion was limited to Kadish C and may support consideration of bilateral skull base resection in selected cases where preoperative imaging demonstrates intracranial extension and tumor proximity to key skull base transition areas. Preserving crista galli integrity during resection facilitates detailed pathological evaluation and may contribute to more accurate staging and prognostic assessment.

paper.title: Cortical thinning and altered directed connectivity in Parkinson's disease: a cortical thickness-guided voxel-wise granger causality study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves both regional cortical degeneration and large-scale network dysfunction. This study examined whether cortical regions showing structural abnormalities in PD also exhibit altered directed connectivity.

METHODS: Sixty-two patients with PD and 46 healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Whole-brain cortical thickness was analyzed using FreeSurfer. Regions showing significant cortical thinning were used as seeds for voxel-wise Granger causality analysis (GCA). Associations between imaging measures and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores were examined using partial correlation analyses.

RESULTS: Patients with PD showed significantly reduced cortical thickness in the right medial superior frontal gyrus (SFGmed.R) and right precentral gyrus (PreCG.R), with no regions showing significantly greater cortical thickness than healthy controls. Compared with controls, patients with PD exhibited increased GCA from SFGmed.R to the left inferior temporal gyrus and from PreCG.R to the calcarine/medial visual cortex, whereas decreased GCA was observed from PreCG.R to the left supramarginal gyrus and from the right superior temporal gyrus and left olfactory-related region to PreCG.R. SFGmed.R cortical thickness was positively associated with MoCA scores after adjustment for age, sex, and education level, and this association remained significant after Bonferroni correction for seven exploratory correlation analyses (partial Spearman's ρ = 0.847, p < 0.001). No other imaging-MoCA associations reached the corrected significance threshold.

CONCLUSION: Cortical thinning in frontal-executive and motor regions of patients with PD is accompanied by altered directed interactions with distributed sensory and associative regions. Medial superior frontal cortical thickness may also be related to global cognitive performance.

paper.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
paper.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological condition primarily caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). However, recent research suggests a functional hyperactivity phase that precedes neuronal degeneration and may hold therapeutic potential. This study was conducted as a narrative review to synthesize evidence on early-phase dopaminergic hyperactivation in PD and different interventions that could potentially delay the onset of PD. We identified various toxins and genetic mutations that increase neuronal excitability, which eventually progresses to depletion of SNc neurons. This disrupts the circuitry of the basal ganglia, resulting in compensatory hyperactivity and increased dopamine release. Preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence supports that neurodegeneration in PD is preceded by a period of neuronal hyperactivation marked by increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, revealing altered striatal connections and increased dopamine turnover. This hyperdopaminergic disorder manifests clinically as early non-motor symptoms like autonomic dysfunction, REM sleep behavior disorder, and hyposmia. Multimodal biomarkers that combine genetic, imaging, and electrophysiological data can detect this pre-degenerative stage, making early intervention possible. Calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory medications that target the NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways are examples of novel strategies for preserving neuronal integrity. Therefore, redefining PD as a disorder of reversible neuronal stress instead of permanent degeneration can lead to opportunities for both early and long-term neuroprotection.

paper.title: The protocol for a phase 2A, multi centre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to assess the effect of 12 weeks treatment with oral PXS-4728A on microglia activation, as measured by positron emission tomography, in participants with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder.

paper.title: Developmental disruption of the mediodorsal thalamus alters prefrontal dopamine D2 receptor expression and prefrontal-accumbal neuronal recruitment during latent inhibition.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The mediodorsal thalamus (MD) is a higher-order thalamic nucleus that plays a central role in the maturation and function of prefrontal cortical circuits. Although developmental MD dysfunction has been implicated in cognitive deficits associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, the underlying molecular and circuit mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether neonatal MD lesions produce persistent alterations in latent inhibition (LI), prefrontal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression, and neuronal recruitment within the MD-prefrontal cortex (PFC)-nucleus accumbens (NAc) circuit.

METHODS: Bilateral excitotoxic MD lesions were induced in Sprague-Dawley rats on postnatal day 4 (MD lesion n = 35; MD Sham n = 35). In adulthood, LI was assessed using a conditioned taste aversion paradigm. Neuronal activation was evaluated by c-Fos immunohistochemistry, whereas D2R expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry, Western blotting, and quantitative PCR. The ability of the D2R antagonist haloperidol to restore LI and neuronal activity was also examined.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Neonatal MD lesions produced a persistent impairment of LI accompanied by reduced task-related c-Fos expression in the PFC and NAc. These functional abnormalities were associated with a selective increase in prefrontal D2R expression at the transcript, protein, and cellular levels, whereas no changes were observed in the secondary motor cortex. Importantly, haloperidol administration during stimulus pre-exposure restored LI and normalized c-Fos activation in the PFC and NAc of MD-lesion animals without affecting sham controls. These findings demonstrate that early MD dysfunction induces long-lasting remodeling of prefrontal dopaminergic signaling and disrupts recruitment of the MD-PFC-NAc circuit during selective attention. They identify altered D2R signaling as a potential mechanism linking developmental thalamic dysfunction to persistent cognitive deficits.

paper.abstract: The convergence of embodied intelligence, neuromorphic computing, and the Internet of Things has propelled intelligent gas sensors to the forefront of artificial olfaction, enabling adaptive, context-aware, and biologically inspired odor perception. Herein, a facile ligand-mediated interfacial co-assembly strategy was developed to construct mesoporous crystalline SnO2/TiO2 composites, which enabled a composition-dependent structural evolution from Sn-substituted TiO2 solid solutions to well-defined n-n heterojunctions. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Sn4+ ions can be substitutionally incorporated into the TiO2 lattice to form charge-balanced Sn-O-Ti bridging units, whereas excessive Sn induces spontaneous phase separation to establish SnO2/TiO2 heterojunctions. The optimized mesoporous hybrids exhibit ~22-fold higher photocurrent and ~4-fold stronger light-motivated ethanol sensing response than pristine mesoporous TiO2 under identical conditions. The outstanding performance was attributed to the site-selective doping that effectively tunes the local electronic structure and promotes the efficient separation and directional transport of photogenerated charges. In situ doping allows for the tailoring and engineering of the pore wall chemical microenvironment, affording an active interface conducive to target gas adsorption and detection reactions. This study establishes a design paradigm for coupling surface reactivity regulation with charge transfer engineering in light-activated gas sensors.

paper.title: Sex differences in clinical profile across Lewy body disease pathology stages.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex impacts clinical profile for people with limbic, neocortical LB pathology, and AD pathology contributes to heterogeneity. Amygdala, olfactory, and brainstem LB can also underlie LB disease and sex differences for these pathology stages are unclear.

METHODS: Data were obtained from National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center for 198 females and 314 males with LB pathology and available data on AD pathology staging. Main and interaction effects of sex and LB pathology group for clinical diagnosis, cognitive, behavioral, and motor outcomes were assessed with logistic and linear regression models, with and without AD pathology staging as a covariate. Sex differences within individual LB pathology groups were also assessed.

RESULTS: Females were less likely to have spouses/partners as informants, had less advanced LB pathology stage, and more advanced ADNC stage. Females were less likely to have RBD and a clinical diagnosis of LB dementia, including after adjustment for AD pathology stage. Advancing LB pathology was associated with a greater reduction in the likelihood of clinical AD diagnosis and a greater increase in the likelihood of auditory hallucinations in males than females, after adjustment for AD pathology stage. Females with neocortical LB pathology were less likely than males to have RBD.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower likelihood of RBD in females was particularly evident at the neocortical LB pathology stage. Clinical correlates of LB pathology may differ by sex, and these sex differences may not be fully explained by AD co-pathology. Considering sex and co-pathology is important for both diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to LB disease.

paper.title: Brain-wide projections of VGLUT2- and Drd2-expressing neurons in the rostral part of the mediodorsal thalamic nucleus of the mouse.
paper.abstract: The rodent mediodorsal thalamic nucleus (MD) includes medial (MDm), central (MDc) and lateral (MDl) segments. In addition, in mice it has a rostral protrusion that occupies the rostral ~ 25% of the whole rostro-caudal MD extension and inherits the name "MD" proper. Vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (VGLUT2) and dopamine receptor subtype 2 (DRD2), encoded by Slc17a6 and Drd2 genes, respectively, are expressed in two genetically defined populations of MD neurons (hereafter MD V GLUT2 or MD Drd2 neurons, respectively). 40 MD VGLUT2 and 13 MD Drd2 neurons located in the rostral protrusion of MD, sparsely labeled by adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors in VGLUT2- and Drd2-Cre mice, respectively, were reconstructed and registered to Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework (CCFv3). Single neurons each projected to multiple brain regions, with the number of projection areas ranging from 2 to 23 or 3-19 within MD V GLUT2 or MD Drd2 ensembles, respectively. The majority of MDVGLUT2 and MD Drd2 neurons connected closely with both striatopallidal structures and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC). Subcortical structures including caudoputamen (CP) and nucleus accumbens (ACB), and anterior olfactory nucleus (AON) received the most frequent innervation and most numerous axon terminations. Pallidal structures such as the bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (BST) and substantia innominata (SI), and olfactory tubercle (OT) and reticular nucleus of the thalamus (RT) were also frequently innervated. Of all the MDVGLUT2 and MD Drd2 neurons projecting to cortex, approximately 77% (37/48) showed close MD-vmPFC connections, and most of these neurons are of matrix type characterized by axon terminations in cortical layers 1-3 (L1-3). Inter-neuron projectomic dissimilarities in MD VGLUT2 and MD Drd2 neuron projectomes distinguished 6 MD V GLUT2 and 2 MD Drd2 neuron subgroups (clusters), respectively. Taken together, the present data revealed a close MD-vmPFC connection pattern which bore strong similarities to the topography of MDm projections in cortex, but not to that of MDc or MDl. Thus, the rostralmost part of "MD" is most likely an MDm continuation. Collectively, MD VGLUT2 or MD Drd2 neurons are integrated into particular, segregated but interdependent MD subnetworks, including PFC-striatopallidal-MD-PFC loops, hence providing morphological substrates for emotion- and cognition-related behavior control.

paper.title: ASAOT: an accentuated structure-differentiated asymmetric optimal transport model for cell type and single-cell spatial mapping.
paper.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) characterizes spatiotemporal gene expression and facilitates analysis of cellular architecture and cell-cell crosstalk within tissue microenvironments. However, existing spatial deconvolution methods employ globally fixed smoothing without local sharpening, which blurs cellular boundaries and impedes reconstruction of layered, heterogeneous cellular patterns in brain tissue. Here, we present Accentuated Structure-differentiated Asymmetric Optimal Transport (ASAOT), a deconvolution framework built on structure-enhanced asymmetric optimal transport. Coupled with spatial neighborhood constraints, ASAOT introduces a differentiated accentuated sharpening term to maintain global spatial continuity, enhance boundary detection, and preserve spot-level expression heterogeneity. Using asymmetric optimal transport, the framework jointly estimates spot-wise cell-type proportions and performs spatial assignment of reference single-cell coordinates. Benchmarks on diverse simulated datasets demonstrate that ASAOT achieves competitive overall accuracy and robustness across moderate spatial resolutions, with the best average comprehensive rank among tested methods. Applications to mouse olfactory bulb and cerebral cortex datasets demonstrate that ASAOT reduces signal diffusion and boundary distortion, effectively recovering layered brain anatomy and stratified cell distributions to build interpretable spatial maps of reference single-cell profiles. Collectively, ASAOT addresses critical drawbacks of conventional methods via a sharpening regularization term, serving as a reliable tool for STs analysis and mechanism exploration of tissue spatial organization.

paper.title: Sex-dependent role of D2-type dopamine receptors in the dorsal hippocampus in social learning and social interactions in mice.
paper.abstract: Social learning is an adaptive and extremely common form of learning that remains poorly understood. Findings with systemic treatments in adult female mice implicated the dopaminergic (DA) system. A D1-type DA receptor antagonist blocked social learning in the social transmission of food preference (STFP) test, whereas a D2-type DA receptor antagonist reduced feeding. A subsequent investigation found that dorsal hippocampus (DH) microinfusions of the D1-type DA receptor antagonist blocked the STFP in male and female mice; however, the role of D2-type DA receptors in the hippocampus in social learning remains unknown. Here, we bilaterally infused the D2-type DA receptor antagonist raclopride (at 10, 14, 18, or 20 μg/μL) or a saline solution (0.9% NaCl) control into the DH of adult male and female CD1 mice prior to the STFP test. Findings revealed a block in social learning in female but not male mice by raclopride at 18 and 20 μg/μL which could not be explained by effects of the drug on total food intake, oronasal investigation (i.e., exposure to the socially carried diet), or olfactory discrimination. Intra-DH raclopride also sex-dependently mediated social interactions, whereby males had a greater reduction in agonistic-type behaviors, whereas females had a greater reduction in social investigatory-type behaviors. This study demonstrates that D2-type DA receptors in the DH sex-dependently regulate social learning and social interactions, with female mice showing greater sensitivity than male mice to D2 receptor antagonism within the dose range tested, highlighting important sex differences in the regulation of social cognition and social interactions.

paper.title: Identification of novel umami peptides from Stropharia rugosoannulata and umami-enhancing mechanism.
paper.abstract: This study discovered and validated novel umami peptides from Stropharia rugosoannulata with intrinsic umami taste and umami-enhancing activity. Peptidomics and machine learning enabled efficient screening of candidate peptides, yielding four peptides (DSPQP, IVDSP, PHRKE, and SLHSK) for detailed analysis. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue (E-tongue) analysis confirmed umami characteristics and revealed lower recognition thresholds than those of monosodium glutamate (MSG). Notably, DSPQP (R = 0.47) and PHRKE (R = 0.49) demonstrated synergistic umami-enhancing effects when combined with MSG. Molecular docking simulations showed stable binding of these peptides to both the taste receptor type 1 member 1/type 1 member 3 heterodimer (T1R1/T1R3) and the transmembrane channel-like protein 4 (TMC4), primarily via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Furthermore, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations suggested that peptide-receptor complexes maintained conformational and binding stability. These findings highlight the umami-enhancing properties and natural flavoring potential of S. rugosoannulata-derived peptides.

paper.title: Effects of salt reduction fermentation on the flavor characteristics of soy sauce.
paper.abstract: Salt-reduced soy sauce represents the growing consumer demand for healthier foods, yet salinity reduction affects flavor perception and microbial metabolic balance. This study systematically investigated how salt reduction affects key enzyme activities, growth and metabolism of Zygosaccharomyces rouxii and Torulopsis versatilis, and associated flavor profiles. Reduced salinity accelerated substrate degradation, elevating total nitrogen (1.68 g/100 mL) and amino nitrogen (1.05 g/100 mL). Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry combined with odor activity value (OAV) analysis indicated that the number of flavor compounds decreased (78), but the total metabolite concentration increased. Compounds contributing to floral, fruity, and malty aromas, including phenylethyl alcohol (OAV: 1.40-2.77), phenylacetaldehyde (OAV: 341.64-404.36), 3-methylbutyraldehyde (OAV: 665.66-1181.45), and 2-methylbutanal (OAV: 143.89-318.77), decreased in OAV. These changes impaired aroma quality and flavor balance, offering insights for optimizing the flavor of salt-reduced soy sauce.

paper.title: Off-flavor formation via non-enzymatic lipid autoxidation in cold-stored potato mash and its inhibition by polyphenols.
paper.abstract: Flavor deterioration of potato mash during storage at 4 °C for 7 days was investigated, focusing on non-enzymatic lipid autoxidation and a polyphenol-based inhibition strategy. Integrating gas chromatography-olfactometry (GC-O) and volatile dynamics, eight characteristic off-flavor compounds derived from polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) oxidation were identified, including hexanal, (E,E)-2,4-decadienal, and (E,E)-2,4-nonadienal. Following thermal inactivation of lipoxygenase (LOX), PUFA degradation was coupled with transient lipid hydroperoxide (LPO) accumulation. Subsequently, Mantel tests and regiospecific cleavage analysis revealed that homolytic β-scission of hydroperoxide intermediates contributes to off-flavor generation, while low temperature kinetically traps (E,Z)-isomers. Furthermore, a defatting model demonstrated the precursor dependence, showing that free fatty acid (FFA) depletion reduced hexanal by >99.6%, attenuating volatile deterioration. Finally, adding tea polyphenol extract (TPE, 0.3 g/kg) reduced lipid oxidation and inhibited these volatiles. These findings provide a scientific basis for off-flavor control and quality preservation in high-moisture starch-based matrices.

paper.title: The neonatal brain surface on cranial ultrasound: Developmental anatomy and clinical implications.
paper.abstract: Cranial ultrasound is the most widely used neuroimaging modality in neonatal intensive care and allows the cortical surface to be followed longitudinally at the bedside; yet, a clinically applicable framework for reading it is lacking. In this narrative review we describe six landmarks-the lateral fissure, insula, sulcus centralis, sulci precentrales and frontales, sulcus cinguli, and sulcus olfactorius-each in terms of anatomy, development, sonographic appearance, and clinical relevance, and each section closing with a bedside summary for pattern recognition. Every landmark is dated twice, on ultrasound and at the postmortem examination; the interval between the two is reported to narrow from about 8 weeks before 28 weeks postmenstrual age to none beyond 31 weeks. Because the thalamus and subplate are central to cortical development, lesions of white and deep grey matter-periventricular leukomalacia and venous infarction complicating intraventricular haemorrhage-may disrupt primary gyration, including altered morphology of the sulcus centralis, whereas direct cortical injury occurs in arterial ischaemic stroke, perinatal asphyxia, sinovenous thrombosis, and meningitis. Altered folding is seen in polymicrogyria, tuberous sclerosis, arhinencephaly, and midline anomalies. Recognizing these landmarks allows cortical maturation to be judged against postmenstrual age, and a cortical lesion to be localized, attributed to a mechanism, and related to the functions it places at risk, including cerebral palsy and cerebral visual impairment.

paper.title: Isoflurane and Surgery Aggravate APOE4-Dependent Lipid Dysregulation, Neural Dysfunction, and Neurological Impairment in Male Mice.
paper.abstract: Perioperative exposure to the volatile anesthetic isoflurane (ISO) during surgery (OP) has been associated with cognitive and olfactory deficits and may increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4), the strongest genetic risk factor for AD, contributes to disease pathogenesis through disrupted lipid homeostasis. However, whether ISO/OP interacts with APOE genotype to influence neurological vulnerability remains unclear. Young adult, presymptomatic humanized APOE4 and APOE3 knock-in mice underwent laparotomy under 2 h of ISO anesthesia. Microglia and astrocytes were isolated from the olfactory bulb (OB) and hippocampus (HI) for lipidomic profiling. Awake in vivo OB recordings assessed neuronal excitability and network activity, while ex vivo patch-clamp recordings assessed synaptic transmission in the OB and HI. On day 7, APOE4/ISO/OP glia showed greater lipid perturbations than APOE3/ISO/OP glia. In vivo recordings revealed genotype-dependent alterations in OB excitability and network operation, while patch-clamp recordings identified altered excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission in the OB and HI. APOE4/ISO/OP mice exhibited persistent odor memory deficits, transient olfactory sensitivity loss, early motor impairment, and delayed cognitive dysfunction. OB RNA sequencing identified alterations in calcium transport and metabolic pathways in APOE4 male mice at 90 days following exposure. Together, these findings demonstrate APOE4-dependent vulnerability to ISO/OP, characterized by glial lipid dysregulation, neural circuit dysfunction, and neurological impairment, and support a potential mechanistic contribution of altered lipid homeostasis.

paper.title: Structural Characterization and Hypoglycemic Mechanism of Pumpkin Seed Polysaccharides.
paper.abstract: This study investigated three pumpkin seed polysaccharide fractions (PSP-1-1, PSP-1-2, and PSP-1-3) with molecular weights of 29,797 Da, 11,209 Da, and 4346 Da, respectively, all containing both α- and β-glycosidic linkages. Structural analysis revealed arabinose, galactose, and glucose as predominant residues in PSP-1-1, while PSP-1-2 and PSP-1-3 additionally contained xylose, with all fractions sharing common structural units. All three fractions were associated with dose-dependent increases in GLP-1 secretion from L cells and with upregulation of genes in the sweet taste receptor pathway. The pooled fraction PSP-1s showed higher gene expression than individual fractions and was therefore selected for in vivo studies. In diabetic mice, PSP-1s intervention alleviated weight loss, reduced hyperphagia and polydipsia, lowered blood glucose, improved glucose tolerance and dyslipidemia, and decreased GSP, insulin, and HOMA-IR while increasing QUICKI. Qualitative histological observations suggested less pronounced pancreatic islet abnormalities following PSP-1s intervention. PSP-1s increased serum GLP-1 concentrations and colonic SCFA concentrations and altered gut microbiota composition. Collectively, the hypoglycemic effects of PSP-1s were accompanied by changes in serum GLP-1, colonic SCFAs, gut microbiota composition, and hypothalamic GLP-1R and appetite-related gene expression. Together with the cellular findings, these observations suggest potential mechanisms involving sweet taste receptor-related signaling and microbiota-associated GLP-1 regulation. However, pathway activation and the causal contribution of gut-brain signaling remain to be established. These findings support further investigation of PSP-1s as a functional food ingredient with potential glucose-regulating activity.

paper.title: Green Coffee Defects and Their Aroma-Relevant Precursors: A Review of Classification Systems, Causal Pathways, and Sensory Chemistry.
paper.abstract: Green coffee defects are evaluated worldwide as visible abnormalities, physical damage, foreign matter, or off-odor, yet the relationship between grading label and cup quality is neither direct nor uniform. This review integrates international and national classification systems with evidence on defect formation, green bean composition, roasting chemistry, and sensory consequences. It shows that standards differ in sample mass, counting basis, legal status, and intended purpose, so their values cannot be converted into a common sensory scale. Defects are best understood as disturbances to precursor pools or as processing and safety risks; they are not fixed flavor entities. Compositional and volatile differences relative to sound coffee are documented for black, sour/brown, immature, insect-damaged, and aged beans; many other visible categories lack defect-specific odor-active or dose-response data. The term quaker illustrates the central nomenclature problem: standards commonly link it to immature beans, whereas a differentiated physiological position treats emaciated beans as a separate pathway. Rio flavor and potato taste defect provide more specific chemical signatures than most visual defects. A precursor-centered framework is proposed to connect grading with analytical and roasting practice while retaining uncertainty where the evidence chain is incomplete.

paper.title: Sensory and Cognitive Modulation of Saltiness Processing in Everyday Food: Evidence from Two fNIRS Experiments.

paper.title: Study on the Effects of Different Drying Methods on Nutritional Quality of Dictyophora rubrovalvata Soup Based on Metabolomics.
paper.abstract: This study investigated the effects of different drying methods on the quality and metabolic characteristics of Dictyophora rubrovalvata soup. Soups were prepared using D. rubrovalvata treated by means of vacuum freeze-drying (FDS), hot-air drying (HADS), far-infrared drying (FIDS), and combined hot-air and far-infrared drying (HAFIDS). The soups, referred to as FDS, HADS, FIDS, and HAFIDS, respectively, were evaluated using an electronic tongue, UV spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and in vitro antioxidant and hypoglycaemic activity assays. By combining these evaluations with non-targeted metabolomics techniques, this study analysed the physicochemical properties, biological activities, and patterns of change in non-volatile metabolites. The spectral results indicated that the Maillard reaction occurred in all groups of D. rubrovalvata soup during the cooking process, with the reaction being more pronounced in the heat-dried group. Among the four soup samples, HAFIDS exhibited superior DPPH radical scavenging, FRAP, and α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities, along with the highest abundance of umami-related metabolites, revealing that combined hot-air and far-infrared drying achieves a favourable balance between flavour and bioactivity. Metabolomics identified a total of 716 metabolites, with 238 differentially expressed metabolites screened, primarily enriched in pathways such as amino acid metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, glucose metabolism, and nucleotide metabolism. Twelve key taste-related amino acids were identified, with significant differences observed between the different drying groups in terms of umami, sweet, and bitter amino acids, as well as organic acids and sugar alcohols. This study systematically investigated the metabolic changes underlying the gustatory quality and bioactivity of D. rubrovalvata soup through a metabolomics analysis of drying methods. It demonstrated that combined hot-air and far-infrared drying is more suitable for the high-value processing of D. rubrovalvata soup, providing a theoretical basis and data support for the flavour optimisation and processing of edible fungus soups.

paper.title: Smart Egg Processing in the Digital Food Era, Part I: Advanced Sensing and Artificial Intelligence for Non-Destructive Egg Quality and Safety Assessment.
paper.abstract: Eggs are still frequently evaluated through periodic destructive tests, while high-throughput processing increasingly requires non-destructive measurements that can support timely decisions. This Part I critical review examines the sensing and prediction layer of smart egg processing, covering computer vision, hyperspectral and multispectral imaging, near-infrared, Raman and fluorescence spectroscopy, electronic-nose sensing, biosensors, and machine-learning methods used to interpret these signals. The evidence shows that no single modality provides complete coverage of external, internal, chemical, and microbiological attributes and that multimodal fusion is no longer merely conceptual: egg-specific studies have demonstrated the fusion of spectral and olfactory information and, more recently, image, shape, and weight features. Explainable AI has likewise entered egg research, including the SHAP-based interpretation of NIR and hyperspectral models. The more persistent limitation is the weakness and inconsistency of validation beyond the development dataset. Small or single-source datasets, incomplete reporting of preprocessing and feature-selection procedures, possible data leakage, class imbalance, limited calibration and uncertainty analysis, and scarce external or prospective validation constrain claims of industrial readiness. The review consequently reframes the central research gap as trustworthy generalization: demonstrating that sensing and AI remain accurate, interpretable, and decision-useful under the biological, environmental, and operational variability of real egg-processing systems.

paper.title: Comparative Analysis of Sauced Beef Based on Electronic Nose, GC-IMS, and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation.
paper.abstract: Sauced beef is a traditional Chinese meat product, yet the volatile and sensory signatures of potential aroma-active compounds remain insufficiently characterized. Five commercial sauced beef products (B1-B5) were analyzed by electronic nose (E-nose), gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS), chemometrics, and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE). Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) identified by GC-IMS were screened by principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA). An FCE model based on texture profile analysis (TPA) was established, with color, taste, flavor, texture, and acceptability as sensory evaluation indicators. E-nose responses indicated that sulfur-containing compounds, aromatic components, alkanes, and alcohols contributed strongly to overall aroma. GC-IMS tentatively identified 73 VOCs, with ketones, alcohols, and aldehydes as the dominant classes. Dual screening (variable importance in projection (VIP) > 1 and odor activity value (OAV) ≥ 1) identified 14 potential aroma-active compounds. Nine compounds were common to all five products, and five were detected in only a subset of products. Under equal weighting, the fuzzy evaluation ranked overall quality as B2 > B4 > B3 = B5 > B1. Pearson correlation revealed that sensory attributes, especially taste and flavor, were positively correlated with 3-(Methylsulfanyl)propanal and (Z)-2-pentenal, while negatively correlated with (R/S)-linalool, 2-Butanone-3-hydroxy, and alpha-Pinene. These integrated approaches revealed differences among the five commercial products investigated, identified potential aroma-active compounds, and support product-specific characteristics and quality assessment of sauced beef products.

paper.title: Thermoresponsive Gel for Sustained Nanoliposome-Mediated Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery.
paper.abstract: Nose-to-brain drug delivery represents a promising non-invasive strategy for improving CNS targeting. However, conventional liquid formulations are limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and short mucosal residence time. ICG-loaded nanoliposomes were prepared using a modified thin-film hydration method and incorporated into a poloxamer-based gel containing hyaluronic acid and Carbomer 940 as mucoadhesive components. The nanoliposomes exhibited a mean particle size of 124 ± 3.25 nm, a unimodal size distribution, and a high ICG encapsulation efficiency of 93.33%. Rheological analysis confirmed a temperature-triggered sol-to-gel transition at the physiological nasal temperature (~32 °C), shear-thinning behavior, and rapid structural recovery suitable for intranasal application. Ex vivo fluorescence imaging in rats demonstrated distinct biodistribution profiles for the ICG-associated signal delivered via the liquid nanoliposomes and gel-incorporated nanoliposomes. Although the liquid liposomes showed faster early signal at 4 h, the gel formulation produced stronger and more sustained brain fluorescence at later time points. At 8 h and 24 h, whole-brain fluorescence was approximately twofold higher with the gel formulation than with the liquid liposomes formulation. These findings indicate that this thermoresponsive gel enhances nasal retention and may modulate the delivery profile of the nose-to-brain transport, supporting its potential as a platform for CNS-targeted delivery and the development of more effective therapies for neurodegenerative diseases.

paper.title: Human Organoids in Radiation Research: Modeling Tissue Injury, Regeneration and Therapeutic Response.
paper.abstract: Radiation therapy is a cornerstone in the treatment of abdominal, pelvic, thoracic, head and neck and central nervous system malignancies. However, irradiation inevitably damages adjacent normal tissues, leading to radiation-induced enteritis, lung injury, cardiac injury, salivary gland dysfunction and brain injury, which compromise both quality of life and treatment outcomes. Traditional two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models have significant limitations in mimicking human tissue radiation responses: the former lacks three-dimensional architecture and cell-cell interactions, while the latter exhibits species-specific differences. In recent years, three-dimensional organoid technology has rapidly emerged as a powerful platform in radiation biology and radiation oncology. In particular, organoids derived from patient tissues or induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) offer key advantages, including self-organization capacity and near-physiological tissue structure and function, which have greatly advanced in-depth research in the radiation field. This review comprehensively summarizes applications of human organoids in radiation injury and regeneration research across the brain, heart, lung, esophagus, salivary gland, intestine, muscle, thyroid, hematopoietic system, and tumors. Animal-derived and organotypic models are included only as comparative or supporting mechanistic evidence and are explicitly identified as such. We focus on advances in modeling radiation injury, elucidating regenerative mechanisms, screening radioprotective and radiosensitizing agents and predicting patient responses to chemoradiation. Current limitations and future directions are discussed collectively at the end.

paper.title: Long-Term Effects of Isoflurane Anesthesia and Surgery: Sex-Associated Neurological Dysfunction and Alterations in Circulating Extracellular Vesicles.
paper.abstract: Volatile anesthetics and surgery can trigger neuroinflammation and neurological dysfunction, but their long-term effects remain poorly understood. Young adult male and female C57BL/6 mice underwent 4 h of 2% isoflurane anesthesia combined with laparotomy (Iso/OP) or sham treatment. At 12 weeks, olfactory and cognitive functions were assessed, followed by RNA sequencing of olfactory bulbs and hippocampi and plasma extracellular vesicle (EV) profiling. EV-associated inflammatory bioactivity was evaluated by hippocampal injection into naïve male mice. Iso/OP induced olfactory deficits at 12 weeks, with greater impairment in females. Female mice also exhibited deficits in spatial working memory and associative learning, whereas males showed relatively preserved cognitive function. Transcriptomic analyses revealed sex-dependent alterations in pathways related to synaptic function, neurodevelopment, extracellular matrix remodeling, stress responses, and chemotaxis. Iso/OP reduced circulating EV abundance, particularly among 40-100 nm particles, and altered EV proteomic profiles. Exploratory analyses of pooled hippocampal tissues revealed distinct cytokine and chemokine profiles following injection of plasma EVs from the four donor groups. Collectively, these findings demonstrate sex-dependent neurological and molecular alterations persisting 12 weeks after Iso/OP, accompanied by changes in circulating EVs. paper.title: Intranasal Chitosan Nano-Formulations: A Novel Frontier in Brain Cancer Therapy.
paper.abstract: Direct nose-to-brain drug delivery is emerging as a promising approach in neuro-oncology because it offers a non-invasive, needle-free route for delivering therapeutics to the brain while partially bypassing the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This approach takes advantage of the natural connections between the nasal cavity and the central nervous system, allowing drugs administered through the nose to reach brain tissues through the olfactory and trigeminal pathways. Despite its potential, successful clinical translation remains challenging because the nasal cavity presents several physiological barriers. Mucus can trap drug molecules, mucociliary clearance can rapidly remove them, and nasal enzymes can degrade them before they reach their target. Advanced nanocarrier systems are therefore being developed to overcome these barriers and improve drug transport through intracellular, paracellular, and transcellular pathways. In this context, specific structural modifications can enhance drug retention, mucus penetration, cellular uptake, and targeting efficiency. Important strategies include the use of mucoadhesive materials such as chitosan to increase residence time in the nasal cavity; hydrophilic coatings such as polyethylene glycol (PEG) to improve movement through mucus; targeting ligands to promote selective cellular uptake; and stimuli-responsive systems that respond to local conditions such as pH, redox state, or glutathione (GSH) levels. These advances are particularly relevant to the treatment of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), one of the most aggressive and difficult-to-treat brain tumors. GBM is characterized by extensive infiltration into surrounding healthy brain tissue, making it difficult to achieve effective drug concentrations throughout both the main tumor mass and its invasive margins. Intranasally delivered chitosan-based nano-formulations may help address this problem through a series of transport steps. After administration, the nanoparticles can interact with and remain within the nasal mucosa, move across the olfactory epithelium, and pass through the cribriform plate toward the olfactory bulb. From there, they may distribute into deeper regions of the brain and potentially increase drug accumulation within both the GBM core and infiltrative tumor regions. This review presents a structured overview of engineered chitosan nano-formulations for targeted drug delivery in neuro-oncology. It focuses on their physicochemical properties, mechanisms of nose-to-brain transport, drug-loading strategies, tumor-targeting approaches, therapeutic applications, and the major challenges that must be addressed before clinical translation. Overall, these systems offer a promising strategy for improving the precision and effectiveness of drug delivery to brain tumors and may contribute to the development of more targeted treatments for GBM and other neurological malignancies.

paper.title: Postoperative opioid-induced respiratory depression monitoring in the context of supplemental oxygen: current limitations and emerging machine-learning approaches.
paper.abstract: Opioid-induced respiratory depression (OIRD) may develop after extubation and remain unrecognized during intermittent postoperative observation. Supplemental oxygen is commonly used to prevent or treat postoperative hypoxemia, but it may preserve peripheral oxygen saturation despite impaired ventilation and thereby delay oximetric warning. Experimental evidence suggests that hyperoxia may also reduce peripheral chemoreceptor drive, although the clinical importance of this effect during routine postoperative low-flow oxygen therapy remains uncertain. This narrative Mini Review examines how supplemental oxygen affects the detection and interpretation of postoperative OIRD, evaluates current respiratory monitoring and machine-learning evidence, and considers requirements for clinical translation. Continuous oximetry and capnography detect more respiratory abnormalities than intermittent assessment, but monitor-defined episodes do not necessarily represent clinically important or opioid-attributable respiratory depression. Their interpretation requires consideration of technical signal validity, clinical significance, and opioid contribution. Existing machine-learning studies have predicted threshold-defined respiratory events, classified individual breaths, distinguished normal from abnormal monitoring segments, or quantified ataxic breathing, supporting the technical feasibility of automated signal interpretation and respiratory phenotype discovery. Among the studies reviewed, none used a prospectively adjudicated clinical OIRD outcome or explicitly modeled oxygen delivery as a time-varying exposure. A testable development pathway would integrate respiratory time series with oxygen delivery, medication administration, and changing clinical context, followed by external validation across devices, institutions, and healthcare settings. Clinical value should ultimately be judged by earlier appropriate intervention and reduced respiratory harm without an unacceptable alarm burden, rather than by improved prediction of threshold-defined episodes alone.

paper.title: Unraveling the formation mechanism of 3-methylindole from tryptophan in the glucose-mediated Maillard reaction: a combined ReaxFF MD, DFT, and experimental study.
paper.abstract: 3-Methylindole is a concentration-dependent aroma compound, and its formation mechanism in the tryptophan-glucose Maillard reaction is crucial for flavor regulation but remains incompletely elucidated. Using gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS), 3-methylindole was identified as a key odor-active compound (OAV > 1). Reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) and density functional theory (DFT) revealed a sequential pathway involving nucleophilic addition, Amadori rearrangement, dehydration, decarboxylation, and Strecker degradation, and characterized 16 transition states and their activation energies, indicating a net endothermic reaction. Pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (Py-GC-MS) detected methylglyoxal and indole-3-acetaldehyde as key intermediates, whose temperature-dependent concentration trends supported the proposed pathway. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further confirmed the multi-stage endothermic behavior, consistent with the DFT results. This study proposes a complete formation mechanism of 3-methylindole, providing a theoretical basis for indole-type flavor generation and a methodological framework for studying volatile compounds in complex thermally processed food systems.

paper.title: White matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
paper.abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder represents a prodromal phase of α-synucleinopathy. Diffusion MRI provides in vivo markers of white matter microstructural properties, while white matter hyperintensities reflect cerebrovascular injury. However, their relative contributions to cognitive and clinical dysfunctions in patients with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder remain unclear. We analysed 168 polysomnography-confirmed isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder participants from the North American Prodromal Synucleinopathy Consortium. Multi-shell diffusion MRI was used to derive metrics from diffusion tensor imaging (fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity) and Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (tissue-weighted neurite density index and orientation dispersion index) across 39 white matter regions using a modified Johns Hopkins University white matter atlas. White matter hyperintensity burden was quantified from fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI. Using linear regression adjusted for age and sex, we compared white matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden between clinically impaired and unimpaired participants and examined associations with multiple cognitive and clinical domains, including global cognition, working memory, motor severity, manual dexterity, autonomic dysfunction, olfactory function, prodromal disease severity and daytime sleepiness. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple comparisons. In our sample (n = 168), participants with clinical impairment (n = 57) demonstrated higher white matter hyperintensity burden than unimpaired participants (n = 111) and showed limited microstructural differences, including lower fractional anisotropy in the superior fronto-occipital fasciculus and inferior occipital white matter and higher orientation dispersion index in inferior occipital white matter. After adjusting for white matter hyperintensity burden, only increased occipital orientation dispersion index remained statistically significant. Diffusion metrics showed widespread associations with digit span forward performance and autonomic dysfunction. In contrast, increased white matter hyperintensity burden demonstrated broader associations with poorer Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores, poorer digit span forward performance, lower Purdue Pegboard performance and higher Prodromal Synucleinopathy Rating Scale scores, indicating greater prodromal disease severity. Our findings highlight cerebrovascular white matter burden as an important correlate of clinical dysfunction in isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder and underscore the need to consider cerebrovascular lesions when interpreting diffusion imaging markers in prodromal synucleinopathy.

paper.title: A comprehensive profiling of active components in Ziziphi Spinosae Semen and its adulterants using instrumental analysis and molecular docking.
paper.abstract: To develop an integrated strategy for differentiating Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (ZSS) from its adulterants, this study combined machine vision, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-IMS), headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), and molecular docking. Machine vision analysis revealed that texture features outperformed color features in distinguishing ZSS from its adulterants. HPLC quantified distinct levels of nine bioactive compounds between ZSS and its adulterants. Combined HS-SPME-GC-IMS and HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis identified terpenes and alcohols as core aroma substances, ZSS and HAS contained far richer volatiles than ZMS and ZJS. Five key odor-active markers were screened via multivariate statistics, whose binding modes with olfactory receptors were interpreted by molecular docking. Collectively, this study systematically clarifies the quality variations across ZSS and its adulterants, laying a reliable theoretical basis for comprehensive exploitation of ZSS products.

paper.title: Functional diversity of GPCR-Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways.
paper.abstract: Gustducin (Ggust), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage Ggust, and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. Here, we develop two complementary biosensors that enable direct monitoring of GPCR-Ggust interaction and downstream signaling in living cells, allowing pharmacological characterization of Ggust activity induced by non-taste GPCRs. We find that several non-taste GPCRs do not activate Ggust but instead stabilize the G protein heterotrimer and suppress basal signaling by forming unproductive GPCR-G protein complexes, whereas others induce conventional Ggust activation and signal transduction. We further show that these unproductive GPCR-Ggust complexes suppress the activation of alternative signaling pathways by sequestering receptors from other G proteins. This mode of interaction functionally partitions GPCRs into activators and inactivators of Ggust and represents a mechanism for balancing concurrent signaling pathways within a cell.

paper.title: Paranasal recesses and rostral airspace volume covary with echolocation call frequency in emballonurid bats.
paper.abstract: The mammalian rostrum has multiple functions including serving as the upper jaw, supporting olfactory sensory structures, conditioning inspired air, and-for some mammals-transmitting sound. Several groups of bats independently evolved bony inflations on the dorsolateral surfaces of their rostra. In rhinolophoid bats, rostral inflations are associated with nasal emission of echolocation calls, but their function in oral emitting bats (family Emballonuridae) is not well understood. Here, we combine μCT, diceCT, and histological methods to describe and quantify nasal fossa morphology of emballonurid bats in a comparative sample of 24 species overall, including 23 in the quantitative CT sample. Our goals are to (1) describe and quantify paranasal recess morphology, (2) explore scaling of paranasal recess size with body, skull, main nasal chamber, and turbinal size, (3) elucidate potential functions of rostral inflations in emballonurids, and (4) understand how nasal fossa morphology is related to presence of socially important glands and odor storing sacs in Emballonuridae. We report surprising diversity, clade-specific traits, and several novelties in paranasal recess size and location among emballonurids. The combined volume of the paranasal recesses and main nasal chamber was more strongly correlated with peak echolocation call frequency used during foraging than with skull size. Some emballonurid species possess a well-developed lateral nasal gland in the lateral recess. Other emballonurids have inflated, air-filled paranasal recesses lined with thin, avascular mucosa, similar to those of nasal emitters with rostral inflations. We also observed turbinal traits reminiscent of those in nasal emitting Rhinolophidae. Proportionally large paranasal recesses are associated with reduced size and turbinal elements in emballonurid bats, except possibly in species that exhibit complex mating displays using perfume storing sacs in their wing membranes. Together, our results suggest that paranasal recesses could play a role in modifying echolocation calls in Emballonuridae, as they are hypothesized to do in nasophonating bats. However, the potential acoustic function of paranasal recesses remains to be experimentally elucidated in bats.

paper.title: Toward the Digitalization of Sensory Analysis of Black Table Olives Using Electronic Nose, Tongue, and Eye.
paper.abstract: Trained sensory panels are the reference for evaluating odor, taste, and appearance, but routine use close to production is limited. This proof-of-concept study evaluated digital support for the sensory analysis of Californian-style black table olives using five electronic sensing blocks. The same 15 cans from three sensory-characterized batches were analyzed using the portable S3+ electronic nose and OECA electronic eye, together with the Integrated Electronic Sensory Analysis Platform (PIASE) at CICYTEX, which incorporates the ASTREE electronic tongue to provide the gustatory domain and, as reference systems, the HERACLES electronic nose and IRIS electronic eye. Can-level PLS-DA balanced accuracies were 1.000 for HERACLES, 0.933 for ASTREE, 0.867 for OECA, 0.867 for IRIS, and 0.533 for S3+. Because each condition was one production batch, these values measure discrimination among three batches, not validation of a general defect classifier. S3+ mean response followed the sensory ordering of off-odor intensity and OECA between-fruit color heterogeneity followed the panel ordering of color uniformity; both are descriptive three-batch concordances. OECA-calibrated color agreed with a CR-400 colorimeter within ΔE00 ≈ 1.2. Mid-level fusion did not outperform the best individual blocks. The results support complementary, domain-specific instruments to assist trained sensory panels rather than replace them.

paper.title: Improving Explosive Detection Dog Performance in Sealed Parcel Searches Through a Targeted Training Intervention.
paper.abstract: Explosive detection dogs are routinely deployed for parcel screening, yet realistic sealed-parcel searches may present challenges not captured by conventional odor-recognition training. In 2025, a black box study of ANSI/ASB Standard 092 identified substantially reduced detection of explosives in tape-sealed parcels, suggesting a potential training gap in this search scenario. This follow-on study evaluated whether brief, progressive training could improve dog performance in sealed-parcel searches. Thirteen operational dog teams participated in trials conducted in Lubbock, Texas, and Miami, Florida. Teams completed a baseline assessment using tape-sealed parcels containing 50 g of C4 or TNT, or distractors, followed by an odor recognition test (ORT) using controlled explosive odor presentations. Following the correction of identified odor-recognition deficiencies, teams completed a training intervention manipulating odor availability through variable parcel venting and requiring progression from odor-source recognition to trained final response. Performance was reassessed using the same parcel configuration. All teams detected C4 during the ORT, whereas only two teams detected TNT. Following intervention, overall sealed-parcel detection sensitivity increased by 35 percentage points (p = 0.0078). C4 detection increased from 38% to 69%, while TNT detection increased from 15% to 54%, although neither individual change reached statistical significance. The results demonstrate that odor recognition does not necessarily translate to effective source localization in sealed parcels and support progressive, operationally representative parcel-search training.

paper.title: Adult predation shapes brain evolution in guppies (Poecilia reticulata).
paper.abstract: Predation is a powerful evolutionary force shaping many traits of prey species. As the brain is the neural substrate of all behaviours, including essential anti-predator actions, its morphology is expected to be directly shaped by predation. However, while correlative evidence supports this relationship, causal evidence of predation driving brain morphology is currently lacking. Here, we investigated how predation pressure changes brain morphology in guppies (Poecilia reticulata) from replicated artificial selection lines for adult predation survival. We found that after three generations of selection, predation-selected females likely evolved relatively larger brains compared to control fish. In males, while brain size was not affected by predation selection, predation lines showed relatively larger olfactory bulbs. These results demonstrate that predation can directly shape the evolution of brain morphology, remarkably fast and in a sex-specific manner. Comparing our findings to those from natural populations with divergent predation pressures allows us to disentangle the direct predation effects from the indirect ecological effects of high predation pressure that drive brain evolution.

paper.title: Giant Sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) Foliar Distillate Elicits Sex-Biased Attraction by the Western Cedar Bark Beetle (Phloeosinus punctatus) in Laboratory Assays.
paper.abstract: Giant sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) is a globally recognized cultural resource and recreational attraction that is listed as 'endangered' on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List. In recent years, the western cedar bark beetle, Phloeosinus punctatus, has been implicated as a contributing factor in giant sequoia crown dieback and mortality of mature trees weakened by drought stress and severe wildfire. However, semiochemical options for monitoring and potentially managing P. punctatus populations are presently unavailable. To address this, we evaluated orientation behavior of P. punctatus to a steam-extracted distillate prepared from giant sequoia branches using Y-tube olfactometry. During olfactometry assays, 45% of adult beetles chose the distillate while 22.5% oriented towards the control arm (32.5% made no choice). Multinomial contrasts indicated that females oriented toward the distillate, whereas males exhibited no preference. Results from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) found the volatile headspace of the distillate to be primarily (> 90%) composed of monoterpenes along with lesser proportions of oxygenated monoterpenoids and relatively non-volatile phenylpropanoids (< 10%), several of which are documented kairomones for conifer-associated insects. Likely kairomones for P. punctatus, the role of females as the host-seeking, pioneering sex, and the potential for giant sequoia distillate and synthetic terpene standards to support monitoring across the natural range of the host tree are discussed.
